knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global-optimality interpretation of the subdifferential residual under convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), \[r_{\partial f}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad0\in\partial f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\operatorname*{argmin}f.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex function, zero subdifferential residual is equivalent to global optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\partial f}(x)=0\iff x\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\).

children.title: Proximal Stationarity Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual measures based on proximal or fixed-point stationarity representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Moreau-Envelope Representation of the Proximal Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth-envelope representation of the convex proximal stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(e_\lambda f(x):=\inf_y\{f(y)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|y-x\|^2\}\), \[
abla e_\lambda f(x)=\lambda^{-1} igl(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x) igr),\qquad r_\lambda(x)=\|
abla e_\lambda f(x)\|.\] The mapping \(
abla e_\lambda f\) is \(1/\lambda\)-Lipschitz and \(\lambda\)-cocoercive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex proximal residual is the norm of the Moreau-envelope gradient, which is globally Lipschitz and cocoercive.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_\lambda(x)=\|\nabla e_\lambda f(x)\|\), and \(\nabla e_\lambda f\) is \(1/\lambda\)-Lipschitz and \(\lambda\)-cocoercive.
knowledge_statements.title: Moreau-Envelope Representation of the Proximal Residual

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_\lambda(x)=0\iff 0\in\partial f(x)\iff x\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex proximal fixed-point residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the single-valued proximal mapping and residual by
\[
p_\lambda(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{f(y)+\frac1{2\lambda}\|y-x\|^2\right\},
\qquad r_\lambda(x)=\frac1\lambda\|x-p_\lambda(x)\|.
\]
The proximal optimality condition gives \((x-p_\lambda(x))/\lambda\in\partial f(p_\lambda(x))\). In particular,
\[
r_\lambda(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=p_\lambda(x)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\partial f(x)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\operatorname*{argmin}f.
\]
Hence the proximal displacement is an exact stationarity residual in the convex setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex function, the scaled proximal displacement vanishes exactly at stationary points, which are precisely global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Stationarity Residuals

children.title: Composite Stationarity Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual representations adapted to composite optimization structures.

assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_\lambda(x)=0\iff 0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial g(x)\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-backward residual for smooth-plus-convex composite objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\operatorname{dom}g\), define
\[
x^+=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda g}(x-\lambda\nabla f(x)),
\qquad G_\lambda(x)=\frac{x-x^+}{\lambda},
\qquad r_\lambda(x)=\|G_\lambda(x)\|.
\]
The proximal optimality condition is
\[
G_\lambda(x)-\nabla f(x)\in\partial g(x^+).
\]
Therefore,
\[
G_\lambda(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=x^+
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial g(x).
\]
Thus the proximal-gradient norm is an exact first-order stationarity residual for the composite objective \(\Psi=f+g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal-gradient mapping is a composite stationarity residual whose zeros are exactly the first-order stationary points of the smooth-plus-convex objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite Stationarity Residuals

children.title: Residual Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where subdifferential and proximal stationarity measures are locally comparable.

assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial(f+g)(x^+))\leq(1+\lambda L)\|G_\lambda(x)\|\leq(1+\lambda L)\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial(f+g)(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative comparison of subdifferential and proximal-gradient residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^+=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda g}(x-\lambda\nabla f(x))\) and \(G_\lambda(x)=(x-x^+)/\lambda\). Proximal optimality gives
\[
G_\lambda(x)+\nabla f(x^+)-\nabla f(x)\in\partial(f+g)(x^+),
\]
so
\[
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial(f+g)(x^+))\leq(1+\lambda L)\|G_\lambda(x)\|.
\]
Firm nonexpansiveness of the proximal mapping also yields
\[
\|G_\lambda(x)\|\leq\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial(f+g)(x)).
\]
Hence subdifferential stationarity and proximal-gradient residuals are quantitatively comparable, with the subdifferential residual evaluated at the forward-backward point in the first inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Lipschitz smoothness and convexity of the nonsmooth term, proximal-gradient and subdifferential stationarity residuals control one another at adjacent iterates.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Equivalence Regimes

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-sided local comparison is stronger than equality of residual zero sets.

children.title: Nonconvex Stationarity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Nonconvex regimes where residual equivalence or solution interpretation becomes limited.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonconvex Stationarity Residual May Lack a Linear Error Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate nonconvex stationarity can make the residual vanish faster than distance to the stationary set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(x)=x^3\), the limiting subdifferential is \(\partial f(x)=\{3x^2\}\), the stationary set is \(S=\{0\}\), and \(r(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))=3x^2\). No finite \(\kappa\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) satisfy
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa r(x)\qquad(|x|<\varepsilon).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the genuinely nonconvex cubic, stationarity violation is quadratic while stationary-set distance is linear, so no local linear error bound exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[S=\{0\},\quad r(x)=3x^2,\quad \nexists\kappa<\infty,\varepsilon>0:\ |x|\le3\kappa x^2\ \forall |x|<\varepsilon.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Stationarity Residual May Lack a Linear Error Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonconvex Stationarity Need Not Imply Minimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing first-order stationarity residual does not certify local minimality in a nonconvex problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(x)=-x^2\),
\[r(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))=2|x|.\]
Thus \(r(0)=0\), although \(0\) is a strict local maximum and not a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero nonconvex stationarity residual can identify a strict local maximum rather than a minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[r(0)=0\quad\text{while }0\text{ is a strict local maximum.}\]
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Stationarity Need Not Imply Minimality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonconvex Proximal Residual May Be Undefined
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Without convexity or suitable prox-boundedness and step-size restrictions, the proximal stationarity representation need not exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g(x)=-x^2\) and \(\lambda>\tfrac12\). For every \(x\in\mathbb R\), the proximal objective
\[u\mapsto -u^2+\frac{1}{2\lambda}(u-x)^2\]
is unbounded below. Consequently \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda g}(x)=\varnothing\), so the single-valued proximal residual \(\lambda^{-1}(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda g}(x))\) is not defined despite smooth stationarity of \(g\) being well defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonconvex function and an excessive step size, the proximal subproblem can be unbounded, so a proximal stationarity residual may not exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda g}(x)=\varnothing\quad\forall x\in\mathbb R.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Proximal Residual May Be Undefined

assumptions_latex: Stationarity is measured by \(r(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\), using the limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There are no constants \(\kappa>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq \kappa r(x)\) whenever \(|x|<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A smooth nonconvex example where stationarity residual vanishes too rapidly for a local linear error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=x^4\), smoothness gives \(\partial f(x)=\{4x^3\}\), so the stationary set is \(S=\{0\}\) and \(r(x)=4|x|^3\). Hence \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)=|x|\). If a local linear stationarity error bound held, then \(|x|\leq 4\kappa |x|^3\) for every sufficiently small nonzero \(x\), equivalently \(1\leq 4\kappa x^2\), which fails as \(x\to0\). Thus first-order stationarity alone does not ensure a linear residual error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the nonconvex function x to the fourth power, the stationarity residual is cubic while distance to the stationary set is linear, so no local linear error bound exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Stationarity Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The concrete example is unsupported and does not match the stated scope: f(x)=x^4 is convex, not nonconvex. A sourced, genuinely nonconvex example is required, and the derivation should not appear as proof text.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A linear inequality system is the feasibility condition \(Ax\leq b\), interpreted componentwise. Its feasible set and natural violation residual are
\[P:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\leq b\},\qquad r_A(x):=(Ax-b)_+,\]
where \(((z)_+)_i:=\max\{z_i,0\}\). Thus \(P\) is a closed convex polyhedron, and feasibility of a point is represented exactly by the zero-residual condition \(x\in P\Longleftrightarrow r_A(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear inequality system has polyhedral feasible set defined by componentwise inequalities, with positive-part constraint violation as its canonical residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Inequality Systems

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual certificate for infeasibility of a finite system of componentwise linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Exactly one of the following systems is solvable:
\[
Ax\leq b,
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\quad y\geq0,\quad b^{\mathsf T}y<0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear inequality system is infeasible exactly when a nonnegative multiplier annihilates the constraint normals and pairs negatively with the right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:Ax\leq b\}=\varnothing\iff\exists y\geq0:\ A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y<0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Farkas Infeasibility Alternative

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hoffman Error Bound for Linear Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical global error bound for consistent finite-dimensional pure inequality systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and fixed finite-dimensional norms, there exists \(H_A<\infty\), depending only on \(A\) and the norms, such that for every \(b\) with \(P(b)=\{z:Az\leq b\}\neq\varnothing\),
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,P(b))\leq H_A\|(Ax-b)_+\|\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^n).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint violation globally controls distance to every nonempty polyhedron represented by a fixed inequality matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists H_A<\infty\ \forall b\text{ with }P(b)\neq\varnothing\ \forall x:\operatorname{dist}(x,P(b))\leq H_A\|(Ax-b)_+\|\).

notation.meaning: an admissible Hoffman bound depending only on A and the chosen norms

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Equality Subsystems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality component of a finite-dimensional mixed linear constraint system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The linear equality subsystem determined by \((A,b)\) has solution set
\[E:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b\}\]
and residual
\[r_E(x):=\|Ax-b\|.\]
The set \(E\) is either empty or an affine subspace, and \(r_E(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\in E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear equality subsystem defines an affine solution set, possibly empty, and the norm of its equality violation vanishes exactly at its solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equality subsystem is satisfied exactly when \(x\in E\), equivalently \(r_E(x)=0\).

notation.meaning: Affine solution set of the equality subsystem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal range test and dual certificate for an equality subsystem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The system \(Ax=b\) is solvable exactly when
\[b\in\operatorname{range}A,\]
equivalently \(AA^\dagger b=b\). If it is not solvable, then there exists \(y\in\mathbb R^p\) such that
\[A^Ty=0,\qquad b^Ty\ne0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality system is consistent exactly when b lies in the range of A; otherwise a left-nullspace vector separates b from that range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b\) is solvable iff \(b\in\operatorname{range}A\) iff \(AA^\dagger b=b\); otherwise \(\exists y\in\ker A^T\) with \(b^Ty\ne0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Equality Consistency Alternative

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projection formula and sharp residual constant for a consistent equality subsystem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(E=\{x:Ax=b\}\neq\varnothing\) and use Euclidean norms. Then
\[P_E(x)=x-A^\dagger(Ax-b),\qquad \operatorname{dist}(x,E)=\|A^\dagger(Ax-b)\|_2.\]
Consequently,
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,E)\le \|A^\dagger\|_2\|Ax-b\|_2.\]
If \(A\ne0\), the least admissible global constant is \(\|A^\dagger\|_2=1/\sigma_{\min}^+(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a consistent equality system, the pseudoinverse gives its Euclidean projection, exact distance, and sharp global residual-bound constant.
assumptions_latex: The domain and residual spaces use Euclidean norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,E)=\|A^\dagger(Ax-b)\|_2\le\|A^\dagger\|_2\|Ax-b\|_2\), with sharp constant \(1/\sigma_{\min}^+(A)\) when \(A\ne0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[S:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b,\ Cx\leq d\}\neq\varnothing.\]
Then a constant \(H<\infty\) exists such that, for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq H\left\|\bigl(Ax-b,(Cx-d)_+\bigr)\right\|.\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best uniform constant for fixed coefficient matrices and residual norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(A,C\) and fixed norms, let
\[S(b,d)=\{x:Ax=b,Cx\le d\}\]
and define
\[H(A,C):=\sup_{\substack{b,d:\ S(b,d)\ne\varnothing}}\ \sup_{x\notin S(b,d)}
\frac{\operatorname{dist}(x,S(b,d))}{\|(Ax-b,(Cx-d)_+)\|}.\]
Then the mixed Hoffman theorem is equivalent to \(H(A,C)<\infty\), and this is the least constant valid uniformly over all consistent right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact mixed Hoffman modulus is the largest distance-to-feasibility/residual ratio over all consistent right-hand sides and infeasible test points.
assumptions_latex: The suprema range only over nonempty feasible sets and points outside those sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H(A,C)<\infty\), and it is the least uniform mixed Hoffman constant.

notation.meaning: Feasible set for the indicated right-hand sides

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided perturbation consequence of a uniform mixed Hoffman constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume the combined residual norm is monotone on nonnegative inequality components. If \(S(b,d)\) and \(S(b',d')\) are nonempty and \(H\) is a Hoffman constant uniform in the right-hand sides, then
\[\operatorname{excess}(S(b,d),S(b',d'))\le H\left\|\bigl(b-b',(d-d')_+\bigr)\right\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a componentwise-monotone residual norm, a uniform mixed Hoffman constant gives a one-sided Lipschitz excess bound under right-hand-side perturbations.

children.title: Constraint-Type Coupling

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Type Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set linear regularity supplies the coupling needed to combine subsystem error bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b\}\), \(I:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Cx\leq d\}\), and \(S:=E\cap I\neq\varnothing\). Suppose that, for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,E)\leq\kappa_E\|Ax-b\|,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(x,I)\leq\kappa_I\|(Cx-d)_+\|,\]
and that the pair \(\{E,I\}\) is globally linearly regular with modulus \(\gamma\), meaning
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\gamma\max\{\operatorname{dist}(x,E),\operatorname{dist}(x,I)\}.\]
Then, for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\gamma\max\{\kappa_E\|Ax-b\|,\kappa_I\|(Cx-d)_+\|\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the equality and inequality feasible sets are globally linearly regular, their individual residual bounds combine into a mixed-system bound whose modulus includes the geometric coupling factor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\gamma\max\{\kappa_E\|Ax-b\|,\kappa_I\|(Cx-d)_+\|\}\).

notation.meaning: Intersection of the equality and inequality feasible sets

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent Mixed Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why the ordinary distance-to-feasibility Hoffman bound requires consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[S:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b,\ Cx\leq d\}=\varnothing\]
and define
\[r(x):=\left\|\bigl(Ax-b,(Cx-d)_+\bigr)\right\|.\]
With \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\varnothing):=+\infty\), no finite constant \(H\) satisfies
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq Hr(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb{R}^n.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a mixed linear system is inconsistent, its feasible set is empty and the ordinary global Hoffman distance bound cannot hold with a finite constant.
assumptions_latex: Distance to the empty set is defined by \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\varnothing)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No finite \(H\) can satisfy \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq H\|(Ax-b,(Cx-d)_+)\|\) for all \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).

notation.meaning: Empty feasible set of the inconsistent mixed system

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Error-Bound Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local conic residual bound represented by metric subregularity of the conic constraint mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^m\) be a nonempty closed convex cone and define
\[S:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax-b\in K\},\qquad G(x):=Ax-b-K.\]
If \(\bar x\in S\) and \(G\) is metrically subregular at \((\bar x,0)\) with modulus \(\kappa\), then some neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) satisfies
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(Ax-b,K)\qquad(x\in U).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric subregularity of the conic constraint mapping is the local property that bounds distance to conic feasibility by distance of the affine image to the cone.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^m\) is a nonempty closed convex cone, \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is linear, and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
The mapping \(G(x):=Ax-b-K\) is metrically subregular at \((\bar x,0)\) with modulus \(\kappa\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For all \(x\) sufficiently near \(\bar x\), \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(Ax-b,K)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a feasible point \(\bar x\), set \(y:=A\bar x-b\in K\). The Robinson condition is
\[A\mathbb{R}^n+T_K(y)=\mathbb{R}^m.\]
Under this condition the conic mapping \(G(x):=Ax-b-K\) is metrically regular at \((\bar x,0)\). In particular, it is metrically subregular there, so constants \(\kappa<\infty\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) exist with
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,G^{-1}(0))\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(Ax-b,K)\quad\text{whenever }\|x-\bar x\|<\varepsilon.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Normal-Cone Form of Robinson Transversality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent primal and polar descriptions of the regular cone-geometry regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^m\) be a closed convex cone, \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear, and \(y\in K\). With the convex normal convention \(N_K(y)=T_K(y)^\circ\),
\[
A\mathbb R^n+T_K(y)=\mathbb R^m
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\ker A^T\cap N_K(y)=\{0\}.
\]
Thus a nonzero \(\lambda\in N_K(y)\) with \(A^T\lambda=0\) certifies failure of Robinson transversality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robinson transversality holds exactly when no nonzero cone normal annihilates the linearized range.

children.title: Nonpolyhedral Extension Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of Hoffman-type control beyond polyhedral geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of a linear conic error bound under tangential contact with a nonpolyhedral cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
K:=\{(s,u,v)\in\mathbb R^3:s\geq\sqrt{u^2+v^2}\},\qquad M(t):=(1,1,t),
\]
and \(S:=\{t\in\mathbb R:M(t)\in K\}\). Then \(S=\{0\}\) and
\[
\operatorname{dist}(M(t),K)=\frac{\sqrt{1+t^2}-1}{\sqrt2}=O(t^2),
\qquad \operatorname{dist}(t,S)=|t|.
\]
Consequently no \(\kappa,\varepsilon>0\) satisfy \(\operatorname{dist}(t,S)\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(M(t),K)\) for every \(|t|<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A line tangent to the second-order cone has quadratic cone residual but linear distance to feasibility, so no local linear error bound holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No local linear constant bounds \(\operatorname{dist}(t,S)\) by \(\operatorname{dist}(M(t),K)\) near zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order-Cone Tangency Failure

assumptions_latex: \(K=\mathbb{S}_+^2\) is the cone of positive semidefinite real symmetric \(2\times2\) matrices.
Matrix distance is measured in the Frobenius norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No constants \(\kappa>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) satisfy \(\operatorname{dist}(t,S)\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(M(t),K)\) for every \(|t|<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangential contact with a nonpolyhedral cone can reduce a linear residual bound to quadratic growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\mathbb{S}_+^2\) and
\[M(t):=\begin{pmatrix}1&t\\t&0\end{pmatrix}.\]
Since \(\det M(t)=-t^2\), the feasible set \(S:=\{t:M(t)\in K\}\) equals \(\{0\}\). The negative eigenvalue is
\[\lambda_-(t)=\frac{1-\sqrt{1+4t^2}}{2},\]
so \(\operatorname{dist}(M(t),K)=|\lambda_-(t)|\sim t^2\), whereas \(\operatorname{dist}(t,S)=|t|\). Therefore no local linear error bound exists. Polyhedral Hoffman behavior does not extend automatically to nonpolyhedral cones without a regularity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A line tangent to the positive semidefinite cone has quadratic cone residual but linear distance to feasibility, precluding a local linear error bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonpolyhedral Extension Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Writing \(S=F^{-1}(\bar y)\) and \(r(x)=\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))\), polyhedral metric subregularity gives constants \(\kappa<\infty\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) for which
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa r(x)\qquad(x\in U).
\]
Thus the Robinson error bound is precisely the solution-distance form of metric subregularity for the polyhedral generalized equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polyhedral generalized equation, metric subregularity becomes Robinson's inequality bounding solution distance by the inclusion residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral-to-Robinson Passage

children.title: Nonpolyhedral Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Loss of automatic bound behavior when polyhedral graph structure is absent.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonpolyhedral family for which the residual decays too rapidly to support a local linear error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any \(p>1\), let \(F_p:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be \(F_p(x)=|x|^p\). Then \(F_p^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\),
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,F_p^{-1}(0))=|x|,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,F_p(x))=|x|^p,\]
and no finite \(\kappa\) and neighborhood \(U\) of \(0\) satisfy
\[|x|\le\kappa |x|^p\qquad(x\in U).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every power map |x|^p with p greater than one is nonpolyhedral and fails metric subregularity at zero because its residual has higher-order decay.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_p\) is not metrically subregular at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Power-Map Failure Family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that leaving the polyhedral class removes the automatic guarantee but does not preclude an error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be \(F(x)=x+x^3\). Its graph is nonpolyhedral, but \(F^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\) and
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(0))=|x|\le |x+x^3|=\operatorname{dist}(0,F(x))\qquad(x\in\mathbb R).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonpolyhedral map x+x³ has a global unit error bound, so nonpolyhedrality is not itself a failure criterion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(0))\le\operatorname{dist}(0,F(x))\) for every \(x\), although \(\operatorname{gph}F\) is nonpolyhedral.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonpolyhedrality Does Not Force Failure
Nonpolyhedral Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of a linear bound for a smooth nonpolyhedral mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(S=F^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\), one has \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)=|x|\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,F(x))=x^2\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R\). There do not exist a finite constant \(\kappa\geq 0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(0\) such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq \kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,F(x))\qquad(x\in U).
\]
Thus \(F(x)=x^2\) is not metrically subregular at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the nonpolyhedral mapping x↦x², solution distance is |x| while the residual is x², and no finite local linear error-bound constant exists at zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No local linear error bound exists at \((0,0)\).

children.title: Hoffman Constants
children.top_down_role: Sharp or admissible residual-to-distance constants for polyhedral systems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal supremum representation of the least uniform Hoffman constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
With zero-residual pairs omitted,
\[
H(A)=\sup\left\{\frac{\operatorname{dist}(x,P(b))}{\|(Ax-b)_+\|}:P(b)\neq\varnothing,\ x\notin P(b)\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Hoffman constant is the worst distance-to-violation ratio over all consistent right-hand sides and infeasible test points.
assumptions_latex: \(H(A)\) denotes the least uniform constant for the fixed matrix and chosen norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H(A)=\sup_{P(b)\neq\varnothing,\ x\notin P(b)}\operatorname{dist}(x,P(b))/\|(Ax-b)_+\|\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Hoffman constant of \(A\) is
\[
H(A):=\inf\left\{H\geq0:\operatorname{dist}(x,P(b))\leq H\lVert(Ax-b)_+\rVert_2\ \text{for every }b\text{ with }P(b)\neq\varnothing\text{ and every }x\right\}.
\]
It depends on the chosen norms and on the inequality representation, but not on a particular feasible right-hand side \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Hoffman constant is the smallest uniform factor bounding distance to any feasible polyhedron by the positive-part violation of its represented inequalities.

children.title: Polyhedral Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of polyhedral feasibility systems as captured by error-bound measures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean feasible-set sensitivity controlled by the Hoffman condition measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P(b)=\{x:Ax\leq b\}\) and suppose \(P(b)\) and \(P(b')\) are nonempty. Then
\[
e(P(b),P(b')):=\sup_{x\in P(b)}\operatorname{dist}_2(x,P(b'))
\leq H(A)\|(b-b')_+\|_2.
\]
Interchanging \(b\) and \(b'\) gives
\[
d_H(P(b),P(b'))\leq H(A)\max\{\|(b-b')_+\|_2,\|(b'-b)_+\|_2\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Hoffman constant bounds one-sided and Hausdorff displacement of nonempty feasible polyhedra under right-hand-side perturbations.
assumptions_latex: \(H(A)<\infty\) is the Euclidean Hoffman constant of the fixed representation.

notation.meaning: one-sided excess of C over D

knowledge_statements.title: Right-Hand-Side Perturbation Bound

assumptions_latex: A finite Hoffman constant \(H(A)\) is fixed for the chosen norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The represented polyhedral system has global linear residual conditioning.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning measured by a global residual-to-distance ratio.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,P(b))\leq H(A)r_b(x).
\]
Consequently, \(H(A)\) is a condition measure for the represented system: small values force residual violation to control geometric infeasibility tightly, whereas large values permit points with small residual but comparatively large distance from \(P(b)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Hoffman constant quantifies polyhedral conditioning by the worst ratio of distance to feasibility over represented constraint violation.

children.title: Dual Characterizations
children.top_down_role: Dual geometric representations used to analyze Hoffman constants.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplier Formula for Distance to a Feasible Polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Euclidean dual representation of distance to a nonempty linear-inequality feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(P(b)=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:Az\leq b\}\neq\varnothing\),
\[
\operatorname{dist}_2(x,P(b))=\max\left\{\lambda^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b):\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m,\ \|A^{\mathsf T}\lambda\|_2\leq1\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to a nonempty inequality polyhedron equals the largest normalized violation aggregated by a nonnegative multiplier.
assumptions_latex: Euclidean distance and norms are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}_2(x,P(b))=\max_{\lambda\geq0,\ \|A^{\mathsf T}\lambda\|_2\leq1}\lambda^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Formula for Distance to a Feasible Polyhedron

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and Euclidean norms are used.
\(\mathcal J(A)\) consists of nonempty row sets \(J\) for which \(A_J\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Hoffman constant equals a maximum of reciprocal dual margins.

notation.meaning: submatrix containing rows indexed by J
dual margin for a row set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean dual-margin formula for an inequality-system Hoffman constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(J\in\mathcal J(A)\), define
\[
\gamma_J:=\min\left\{\lVert A_J^{\mathsf T}v\rVert_2:v\in\mathbb R_+^{J},\ \lVert v\rVert_2=1\right\}.
\]
Full row rank gives \(\gamma_J>0\). The Euclidean Hoffman constant admits the dual characterization
\[
H(A)=\max_{J\in\mathcal J(A)}\gamma_J^{-1},
\]
with redundant or inactive row families removed through the maximization over admissible subsystems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Euclidean Hoffman constant is the largest reciprocal dual margin among full-row-rank subsystems of the inequality matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Characterizations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An authoritative source is required for the exact maximum formula. Restricting admissible subsystems merely to full-row-rank row sets may be stronger than the standard dual admissibility condition and can change the asserted characterization.

children.title: Representation Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of conditioning measures on the chosen constraint representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of Hoffman conditioning on positive row scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d_{\min}=\min_{1\leq i\leq m}d_i\) and \(d_{\max}=\max_{1\leq i\leq m}d_i\). The systems \(Ax\leq b\) and \(DAx\leq Db\) define the same feasible set. Their Euclidean residuals satisfy
\[
d_{\min}\lVert(Ax-b)_+\rVert_2\leq\lVert D(Ax-b)_+\rVert_2\leq d_{\max}\lVert(Ax-b)_+\rVert_2
\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^n),
\]
and their least uniform Hoffman constants satisfy
\[
\frac{H(A)}{d_{\max}}\leq H(DA)\leq\frac{H(A)}{d_{\min}}.
\]
Hence the Hoffman constant depends on the chosen inequality representation and residual scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive row scaling preserves the represented feasible polyhedron but can change its Hoffman constant, with the change bounded by the smallest and largest row scales.
assumptions_latex: Euclidean residual norms are used for the equivalent systems \(Ax\leq b\) and \(DAx\leq Db\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equivalent positive row scalings can change the Hoffman constant only within the stated scaling bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Redundant Duplication Changes the Euclidean Hoffman Constant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected claim about the matrix-uniform Hoffman constant for duplicated rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The proposed identity \(H(A_q)=q^{-1/2}\) for the \(q\)-row all-ones matrix is false under the standard definition uniform over all consistent right-hand sides. Although tying all duplicated right-hand sides together scales that restricted residual by \(\sqrt q\), arbitrary right-hand sides are allowed in \(H(A_q)\); choosing a unique smallest component yields a distance-to-residual ratio equal to \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicating rows does not give the claimed one-over-square-root-q matrix-uniform Hoffman constant because the uniform definition permits unequal right-hand sides.
assumptions_latex: \(A_q\in\mathbb R^{q\times1}\) has every entry equal to one.
The Hoffman constant is uniform over every consistent \(b\in\mathbb R^q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H(A_q)=1\), not \(q^{-1/2}\), for the standard matrix-uniform definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Duplication Changes the Euclidean Hoffman Constant

intermediate_metadata.reason: The locally owned inventory is the immutable positive-row-scaling law, which already demonstrates representation dependence and gives sharp comparison bounds. The builder's redundant-duplication formula is deferred because it confuses tied right-hand sides with the standard constant uniform over arbitrary right-hand sides. Definitions, dual formulas, general conditioning, and genuinely ill-conditioned matrix families are excluded to sibling leaves.

children.title: Ill-Conditioned Polyhedral Regimes
children.top_down_role: Geometric configurations associated with large or unstable Hoffman constants.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalized Witnesses of Diverging Hoffman Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal sequential certificate for absence of a uniform Hoffman bound across a fixed-dimensional family of represented systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a fixed-dimensional sequence of matrices \(A_k\),
\[
\sup_k H(A_k)=+\infty
\]
if and only if, after passage to a subsequence if necessary, there are consistent right-hand sides \(b_k\) and points \(x_k\notin P_k:=\{x:A_kx\leq b_k\}\) such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x_k,P_k)=1,
\qquad
\|(A_kx_k-b_k)_+\|\longrightarrow0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family is arbitrarily ill-conditioned exactly when unit-distance infeasible points can have represented violations tending to zero.
assumptions_latex: The matrices \(A_k\) have common finite dimensions.
Each witness polyhedron \(P_k=\{x:A_kx\leq b_k\}\) is nonempty.
The same homogeneous norms are used throughout the family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_kH(A_k)=+\infty\iff\exists(b_k,x_k):\operatorname{dist}(x_k,P_k)=1,\ \|(A_kx_k-b_k)_+\|\to0\).

notation.meaning: feasible polyhedron for the kth witness system

knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Witnesses of Diverging Hoffman Conditioning

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nearly Opposing Normals Produce Diverging Constants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit primal witness family showing loss of uniform conditioning as two inequality normals become nearly opposite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
A_\varepsilon=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-1&\varepsilon\end{pmatrix},\qquad b=0,\qquad \varepsilon>0.
\]
For \(x=(0,1)\), the feasible wedge \(P_\varepsilon=\{z:A_\varepsilon z\leq0\}\) satisfies
\[
\operatorname{dist}_2(x,P_\varepsilon)=1,
\qquad
\|(A_\varepsilon x)_+\|_2=\varepsilon.
\]
Consequently \(H(A_\varepsilon)\geq\varepsilon^{-1}\to+\infty\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), although every fixed positive-\(\varepsilon\) system has a finite Hoffman constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two nearly opposing constraint normals yield unit-distance infeasible points with residual size epsilon, forcing the Hoffman constants to diverge.
assumptions_latex: Euclidean distance and residual norms are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H(A_\varepsilon)\geq1/\varepsilon\to+\infty\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).

notation.meaning: feasible wedge defined by the nearly opposing normals

knowledge_statements.title: Nearly Opposing Normals Produce Diverging Constants

assumptions_latex: Euclidean norms define the Hoffman constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family becomes arbitrarily ill-conditioned as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Divergence caused by nearly cancelling active normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the dual vector \(v=(1,1)/\sqrt2\),
\[
\lVert A_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}v\rVert_2=\frac{\varepsilon}{\sqrt2}.
\]
The dual-margin characterization consequently yields
\[
H(A_\varepsilon)\geq\frac{\sqrt2}{\varepsilon}\longrightarrow+\infty
\qquad\text{as }\varepsilon\downarrow0.
\]
Thus each positive-\(\varepsilon\) system is polyhedral and has a finite error-bound constant, yet nearly cancelling constraint normals make the family uniformly ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearly opposing constraint normals make Hoffman constants diverge, although every fixed member of the polyhedral family still has a finite error bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Polyhedral Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed calculation suggests the claimed divergence, but the conclusion relies on the preceding unvalidated dual characterization and is presented as a proof. A source validating the applicable Hoffman dual formula is required before a reliable replacement can be issued.

children.top_down_role: Residual bounds for monotone, affine, and nonlinear variational inequalities.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projected residual gives a global error bound for the variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strongly monotone finite-dimensional variational inequality with projected residual.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 Sensitivity Analysis for Variational Systems p. 421
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The variational inequality
\[
\langle F(x^*),x-x^*\rangle\geq0\qquad(x\in C)
\]
has a unique solution \(x^*\). With \(q=\sqrt{1-2\alpha\mu+\alpha^2L^2}<1\), every \(x\in C\) satisfies
\[
\lVert x-x^*\rVert_2\leq\frac{1}{1-q}\lVert r_\alpha(x)\rVert_2.
\]
Hence the computable projected residual globally controls distance to the solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strongly monotone Lipschitz variational inequality, the projected residual globally bounds distance to the unique solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Variational-Inequality Error Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4 Sensitivity Analysis for Variational Systems p. 421

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional variational inequality over a nonempty closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(F:C\to\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\alpha>0\). For \(x\in C\),
\[\langle F(x),z-x\rangle\ge0\quad(z\in C)\]
is equivalent to
\[0\in F(x)+N_C(x),\]
and to
\[r_\alpha(x):=x-P_C(x-\alpha F(x))=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point solves the variational inequality exactly when it solves its normal-cone inclusion, equivalently when its projected residual vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\operatorname{SOL}(F,C)\iff0\in F(x)+N_C(x)\iff r_\alpha(x)=0.\)

notation.meaning: convex normal cone to C at x

children.title: Complementarity Error Bounds
children.top_down_role: Residual bounds for linear, nonlinear, mixed, and conic complementarity systems.

assumptions_latex: For \(q\in\mathbb R^n\), the linear complementarity problem seeks \(x\geq0\), \(Mx+q\geq0\), and \(x^{\mathsf T}(Mx+q)=0\).
The componentwise minimum residual is measured in a fixed norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The natural complementarity residual satisfies a global error bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global natural-residual bound for a P-matrix linear complementarity problem.

source_refs.locator: 5.10 Residues and Error Bounds p. 475
source_refs.source_title: The Linear Complementarity Problem

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(q\), the \(P\)-matrix linear complementarity problem has a unique solution \(x^*(q)\). Moreover, there exists \(\kappa_M<\infty\), depending only on \(M\) and the selected norm, such that for every \(q\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(x\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
\lVert x-x^*(q)\rVert\leq\kappa_M\lVert\min\{x,Mx+q\}\rVert.
\]
The minimum is taken componentwise and vanishes exactly at complementary feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a P-matrix linear complementarity problem, the componentwise minimum residual globally controls distance to the unique solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity Error Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: 5.10 Residues and Error Bounds p. 475
source_witnesses.source_title: The Linear Complementarity Problem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local error bound for a locally Lipschitz complementarity residual in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\), with \(R(\bar x)=0\). If every \(A\in\partial_C R(\bar x)\) is nonsingular, then \(R\) has a locally Lipschitz inverse near \((\bar x,0)\). In particular, for some neighborhood \(U\) and \(\kappa<\infty\), \[\|x-\bar x\|\le\kappa\|R(x)\|\qquad(x\in U).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsingularity of every Clarke generalized Jacobian matrix of an exact complementarity residual certifies local isolation and a local error bound.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\) and \(R(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There are \(U\) and \(\kappa\) such that \(\|x-\bar x\|\le\kappa\|R(x)\|\) for every \(x\in U\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsingular Generalized-Jacobian Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Residual Need Not Give a Linear Error Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar nonlinear-complementarity boundary caused by a flat natural residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider complementarity on \(K=\mathbb R_+\) with \(F(x)=x^2\). Its solution set is \(\Omega=\{0\}\), and the natural residual is \(R(x)=x-\max\{0,x-x^2\}\). For \(0<x<1\), \(R(x)=x^2\), so \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\Omega)/|R(x)|=1/x\to\infty\). Hence no local linear error bound holds at \(0\), although \(R^{-1}(0)=\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complementarity residual may identify solutions exactly yet be too flat to control distance linearly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No finite \(\kappa\) satisfies \(|x|\le\kappa|R(x)|\) throughout a neighborhood of \(0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Residual Need Not Give a Linear Error Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local and Global Complementarity Error Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual formulation common to nonlinear, mixed, and conic complementarity systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\) be the solution set of a complementarity system and let \(R\) satisfy \(R(z)=0\iff z\in\Omega\). A local complementarity error bound at \(\bar z\in\Omega\) is \[\operatorname{dist}(z,\Omega)\le\kappa\|R(z)\|\] for all \(z\) near \(\bar z\). It is global on \(D\) when one finite \(\kappa\) works for every \(z\in D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complementarity error bound controls distance to the complete solution set by an exact complementarity residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(z,\Omega)\le\kappa\|R(z)\|\) locally or globally on the specified domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Local and Global Complementarity Error Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection representation for complementarity over a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty closed convex cone and define \(R_K(x):=x-\Pi_K(x-F(x))\). Then \[R_K(x)=0\iff x\in K,\quad F(x)\in K^*,\quad \langle x,F(x)\rangle=0.\] Thus \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\Omega)\le\kappa\|R_K(x)\|\) is a conic complementarity error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conic complementarity is exactly the zero set of its natural projection residual.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_K(x)=0\) exactly at complementary pairs \(x\in K\), \(F(x)\in K^*\), and \(\langle x,F(x)\rangle=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Natural Residual for Conic Complementarity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Box-projection representation of a finite-dimensional mixed complementarity problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\), allowing infinite endpoints, and define \(R_C(x):=x-\Pi_C(x-F(x))\). Then \(R_C(x)=0\) exactly when, coordinatewise, \[\ell_i<x_i<u_i\Rightarrow F_i(x)=0,\qquad x_i=\ell_i\Rightarrow F_i(x)\ge0,\qquad x_i=u_i\Rightarrow F_i(x)\le0.\] Consequently \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\Omega)\le\kappa\|R_C(x)\|\) is a mixed-complementarity error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box projection residual vanishes exactly at mixed-complementarity solutions and supplies their natural error-bound residual.
assumptions_latex: \(C=[\ell,u]\) is a nonempty box in \(\mathbb R^n\), possibly with infinite endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_C^{-1}(0)\) is exactly the mixed-complementarity solution set.
knowledge_statements.title: Natural Residual for Mixed Complementarity

children.title: KKT Error Bounds
children.top_down_role: Residual-to-distance estimates for Karush–Kuhn–Tucker solution sets.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{dist}(z,S)\le \kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(0,K(z))\quad(z\in U).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local set-valued residual formulation near a fixed KKT pair.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.3 Local uniqueness in terms of KKT triples p. 279
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A local KKT error bound at \(\bar z\) holds if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar z\) and \(\kappa\ge 0\) such that
\[\operatorname{dist}(z,S)\le \kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(0,K(z))\quad\text{for every }z\in U.\]
Equivalently, \(K\) is metrically subregular at \((\bar z,0)\). The distance on the left is to the entire local KKT solution set, so the definition does not require an isolated primal-dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A KKT error bound controls distance to the full KKT solution set by the size of a chosen primal-dual residual near a reference KKT pair.
knowledge_statements.title: KKT Error Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.3 Local uniqueness in terms of KKT triples p. 279
source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. I

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Natural Residual for a Smooth NLP KKT System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact single-valued residual for smooth equality-and-inequality constrained programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)\le0\) and \(h(x)=0\), with multipliers \(\lambda\ge0\) and \(\mu\). Define \[R(x,\lambda,\mu):= igl(
abla f(x)+
abla g(x)^\mathsf T\lambda+
abla h(x)^\mathsf T\mu,\ h(x),\ \min\{-g(x),\lambda\} igr),\] where the minimum is componentwise. Then \(R(x,\lambda,\mu)=0\) exactly when stationarity, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity hold. Thus a local KKT error bound can be written \[\operatorname{dist}((x,\lambda,\mu),S)\le\kappa\|R(x,\lambda,\mu)\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth nonlinear program, stationarity, equality feasibility, and a componentwise minimum form one exact KKT residual.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g,h\) are continuously differentiable near the reference point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R^{-1}(0)=S\), the KKT solution set.
knowledge_statements.title: Natural Residual for a Smooth NLP KKT System

children.title: Primal Error Bounds
children.top_down_role: Residual control directed at the primal solution component.

assumptions_latex: The local KKT error bound of node \(A03.SC05.N34D37239A396.ANDD808E86F72\) holds with modulus \(\kappa\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le \kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(0,K(x,\lambda)).\]

notation.meaning: projection of the KKT set onto primal space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection of a coupled KKT bound onto the primal variables.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.3 Local uniqueness in terms of KKT triples p. 279
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \((x,\lambda)\), projection cannot increase distance:
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le \operatorname{dist}((x,\lambda),S).\]
Consequently, wherever the local KKT error bound is valid,
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le \kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(0,K(x,\lambda)).\]
Thus a coupled residual certifies primal proximity even when the multiplier associated with a nearby primal solution is not unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting a KKT error bound yields a primal bound: distance to primal solutions is at most the coupled residual times the same modulus.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Error Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.3 Local uniqueness in terms of KKT triples p. 279
source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. I

children.title: Dual Error Bounds
children.top_down_role: Residual control directed at multiplier or dual solution components.

assumptions_latex: The local KKT error bound holds near \((\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) with modulus \(\kappa\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{dist}(\lambda,\Lambda^*)\le \kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(0,K(x,\lambda)).\]

notation.meaning: projection of the KKT set onto multiplier space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection of a coupled KKT bound onto multiplier space.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.3 Local uniqueness in terms of KKT triples p. 279
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \((x,\lambda)\), projection onto multiplier space gives
\[\operatorname{dist}(\lambda,\Lambda^*)\le \operatorname{dist}((x,\lambda),S).\]
Hence the local KKT error bound implies
\[\operatorname{dist}(\lambda,\Lambda^*)\le \kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(0,K(x,\lambda)).\]
This estimates distance to the multiplier solution set; a bound to one designated multiplier requires additional isolation or uniqueness assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled KKT bound controls distance to the multiplier solution set, but generally not distance to one selected multiplier.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Error Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.3 Local uniqueness in terms of KKT triples p. 279
source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. I

children.title: Coupled Primal-Dual Bounds
children.top_down_role: Joint residual control for combined primal and multiplier solution sets.

assumptions_latex: \(X^*\) and \(\Lambda^*\) are the primal and multiplier projections of a nonempty KKT set \(S\).
A local KKT error bound holds with modulus \(\kappa\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\bigl(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^2+\operatorname{dist}(\lambda,\Lambda^*)^2\bigr)^{1/2}\le \sqrt{2}\,\kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(0,K(x,\lambda)).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint consequence of the primal and dual projection bounds.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.3 Local uniqueness in terms of KKT triples p. 279
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The primal and dual projection inequalities imply
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^2+\operatorname{dist}(\lambda,\Lambda^*)^2\le 2\operatorname{dist}((x,\lambda),S)^2.\]
Therefore, near the reference KKT pair,
\[\bigl(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^2+\operatorname{dist}(\lambda,\Lambda^*)^2\bigr)^{1/2}\le \sqrt{2}\,\kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(0,K(x,\lambda)).\]
This product-of-projections bound is weaker than distance to \(S\), because not every pairing from \(X^*\times\Lambda^*\) need be a KKT pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A KKT residual jointly controls primal and multiplier projection distances, although the product of the two projection sets may exceed the KKT set.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Primal-Dual Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.3 Local uniqueness in terms of KKT triples p. 279
source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. I

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct joint projection consequence of a KKT-set error bound in the Euclidean product norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq X^*\times\Lambda^*\) be the KKT set and equip the primal-dual space with the Euclidean product norm. Then \[\operatorname{dist}((x,\lambda),X^*\times\Lambda^*)=\bigl(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^2+\operatorname{dist}(\lambda,\Lambda^*)^2\bigr)^{1/2}\le\operatorname{dist}((x,\lambda),S).\] Hence any KKT error bound with modulus \(\kappa\) yields the same-modulus joint projection bound \[\bigl(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^2+\operatorname{dist}(\lambda,\Lambda^*)^2\bigr)^{1/2}\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,K(x,\lambda)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because the KKT set lies inside the product of its projections, the full KKT error bound controls the two projection distances jointly with the same modulus, not merely a square-root-of-two enlargement.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a nonempty KKT set with projections \(X^*\) and \(\Lambda^*\).
The primal-dual space uses the Euclidean product norm.
A local KKT error bound holds with modulus \(\kappa\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^2+\operatorname{dist}(\lambda,\Lambda^*)^2\bigr)^{1/2}\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,K(x,\lambda))\).

notation.meaning: primal and multiplier projections of the KKT set

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Product-of-Projections Bound

children.title: Multiplier Nonuniqueness Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limitations on dual or joint error bounds caused by nonunique multipliers.

assumptions_latex: Consider minimizing the zero function subject to \(h_1(x)=x=0\) and \(h_2(x)=x=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Lambda(0)=\{(t,-t):t\in\mathbb{R}\},\qquad |\lambda-\bar\lambda|\le c\,|\lambda_1+\lambda_2|\ \text{fails locally for every }c.\]

notation.meaning: multiplier set at the feasible point

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit duplicated-equality counterexample is directly checkable
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duplicated equality constraints expose the boundary created by nonunique multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Stationarity is \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2=0\), so
\[\Lambda(0)=\{(t,-t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}.\]
Fix \(\bar\lambda=(0,0)\). Along \(\lambda=(t,-t)\), the stationarity residual \(|\lambda_1+\lambda_2|\) is zero while \(|\lambda-\bar\lambda|=\sqrt{2}|t|\). Thus no finite \(c\) yields a local bound \(|\lambda-\bar\lambda|\le c|\lambda_1+\lambda_2|\). A set-valued bound using \(\operatorname{dist}(\lambda,\Lambda(0))\) is not contradicted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicating an equality constraint creates a line of multipliers, so a zero stationarity residual cannot bound distance to one selected multiplier.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Nonuniqueness Boundary

children.title: Piecewise Polyhedral Inclusion Bounds
children.top_down_role: Error bounds derived from finite polyhedral structure in generalized equations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional finite-union convention for piecewise-polyhedral graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multifunction \(F:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\) is piecewise polyhedral when \(\operatorname{gph}F\) is the union of finitely many convex polyhedra in \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional multifunction is piecewise polyhedral when its graph is a finite union of convex polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{gph}F=\bigcup_{i=1}^N P_i\) for finitely many convex polyhedra \(P_i\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Piecewise-Polyhedral Multifunction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A countable polyhedral decomposition accumulating at the reference point need not yield an error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(F:\mathbb R\rightrightarrows\mathbb R\) by \(F(0)=\{0\}\), \(F(1/n)=\{1/n^2\}\) for \(n\in\mathbb N\), and \(F(x)=\varnothing\) otherwise. Its graph is a countable union of singleton polyhedra, but at \((0,0)\), \[\frac{\operatorname{dist}(1/n,F^{-1}(0))}{\operatorname{dist}(0,F(1/n))}=n.\] Hence \(F\) is not metrically subregular at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infinite polyhedral decomposition whose pieces accumulate at the reference point can fail to provide any local linear error bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{gph}F\) is a countable union of polyhedra, but \(F\) is not metrically subregular at \((0,0)\).

notation.meaning: solution set for the reference inclusion

knowledge_statements.title: Failure Without Local Finiteness

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(\bar y))\le \kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))\quad(x\in U).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local bound for a piecewise polyhedral multifunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(\kappa\ge 0\) such that
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(\bar y))\le \kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))\quad\text{for every }x\in U.\]
Thus every finite-dimensional piecewise polyhedral multifunction is metrically subregular at each point of its graph. Applied to the inclusion \(\bar y\in F(x)\), this gives a local Lipschitz error bound derived solely from the finite polyhedral graph structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional piecewise polyhedral inclusion admits a local error bound at every graph point, with solution distance controlled by inclusion residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise Polyhedral Inclusion Bounds

children.top_down_role: The mapping-theoretic organization of local residual bounds.

children.title: Metric Subregularity Formulation
children.top_down_role: The mapping-theoretic viewpoint on fixed-target residual control.

assumptions_latex: \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) is a multifunction between metric spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(\bar y))\le \kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))\quad(x\in U).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard metric-space definition at one fixed graph point.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.3 Metric Regularity and Covering p. 56
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The mapping \(F\) is metrically subregular at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(\kappa\ge 0\) such that
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(\bar y))\le \kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))\quad\text{for every }x\in U.\]
The convention is \(\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,\varnothing)=+\infty\), so the inequality remains meaningful when \(F(x)\) is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric subregularity bounds distance to the inverse image of a fixed value by the residual distance from that value to the mapping.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric Subregularity Formulation

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.3 Metric Regularity and Covering p. 56
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least constant valid in the fixed-target subregularity estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The exact metric-subregularity modulus of \(F\) at \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\) is
\[\operatorname{subreg}F(\bar x\mid\bar y):=\inf\{\kappa\ge0:\exists U\ni\bar x,\ \operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(\bar y))\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))\ \forall x\in U\}.\]
It is \(+\infty\) if no finite admissible constant exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact subregularity modulus is the infimum of all constants valid in the fixed-target local distance estimate.
assumptions_latex: \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) is a multifunction between metric spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{subreg}F(\bar x\mid\bar y)=\inf\{\kappa:\kappa\text{ is locally admissible}\}.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Metric-Subregularity Modulus

children.title: Local Error-Bound Formulation
children.top_down_role: The residual-to-solution-distance viewpoint near a reference solution.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le \kappa r(x)\quad(x\in U).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical local error bound for a set-valued inclusion.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.3 Metric Regularity and Covering p. 56
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The inclusion \(\bar y\in F(x)\) has a local Lipschitz error bound at \(\bar x\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(\kappa\ge 0\) satisfying
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le \kappa r(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in U,\]
where \(S=F^{-1}(\bar y)\) and \(r(x)=\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))\). The residual vanishes exactly on \(S\) whenever the values of \(F\) are closed near the reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local inclusion error bound controls distance to the solution set by the canonical residual measuring violation of the inclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Error-Bound Formulation

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.3 Metric Regularity and Covering p. 56
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least asymptotic constant in the canonical residual inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(S=F^{-1}(\bar y)\) and \(r(x)=\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))\), define
\[\operatorname{eb}(r;\bar x):=\inf\{\kappa\ge0:\exists U\ni\bar x,\ \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa r(x)\ \forall x\in U\}.\]
With extended-real ratio conventions,
\[\operatorname{eb}(r;\bar x)=\limsup_{\substack{x\to\bar x\\x\notin S}}\frac{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)}{r(x)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact local error-bound modulus is the least valid local constant, equivalently the limiting upper ratio of solution distance to residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{eb}(r;\bar x)=\inf\kappa=\limsup_{x\to\bar x,\ x\notin S}\frac{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)}{r(x)}.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Local Error-Bound Modulus

children.title: Subregularity–Error-Bound Correspondence
children.top_down_role: The local equivalence between mapping subregularity and residual error bounds.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F\text{ is metrically subregular at }(\bar x,\bar y)\iff \exists U,\kappa:\ \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa r(x)\ \forall x\in U.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence for the canonical distance residual.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.3 Metric Regularity and Covering p. 56
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Metric subregularity of \(F\) at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is equivalent to the local error bound for its canonical residual:
\[F\text{ is metrically subregular at }(\bar x,\bar y)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists U,\kappa\ge0:\ \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa r(x)\ \forall x\in U.\]
The two statements have the same admissible moduli because \(S=F^{-1}(\bar y)\) and \(r(x)=\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))\); the correspondence is an identity of formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric subregularity is exactly the local error-bound property when violation is measured by the canonical distance to the multifunction value.
knowledge_statements.title: Subregularity–Error-Bound Correspondence

children.title: Residual Representation Dependence
children.top_down_role: How the chosen residual mapping affects the expression and modulus of the equivalence.

assumptions_latex: \(r(x)=\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))\) is the canonical residual near \(\bar x\).
Another residual \(\rho\ge0\) has the same local zero set and satisfies \(a r(x)\le\rho(x)\le b r(x)\) for some \(a,b>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa r(x)\Rightarrow\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le(\kappa/a)\rho(x),\qquad \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le c\rho(x)\Rightarrow\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le cb\,r(x).\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: inequalities follow directly from local two-sided residual comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of error bounds under local two-sided residual equivalence.

source_refs.locator: 4.1.2 Neighborhood Characterizations of Metric Regularity and Lipschitzian Behavior p. 382
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(a r(x)\le\rho(x)\le b r(x)\) locally for constants \(a,b>0\), then a local error bound expressed with either residual transfers to the other. Specifically,
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa r(x)\ \Longrightarrow\ \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le(\kappa/a)\rho(x),\]
and
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le c\rho(x)\ \Longrightarrow\ \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le cb\,r(x).\]
Equality of zero sets alone is insufficient; the local comparison rates determine whether a Lipschitz error bound is preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Error bounds transfer between locally comparable residuals, with rescaled moduli; merely sharing the same zero set does not ensure equivalence.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Representation Dependence

children.title: Equivalence Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Settings where localization, solution-set choice, or residual mismatch obstructs the correspondence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonclosed values can make canonical distance vanish without actual inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R\rightrightarrows\mathbb R\) satisfy \(F(0)=\{0\}\) and \(F(x)=(0,1)\) for \(x\ne0\), with \((\bar x,\bar y)=(0,0)\). Then \(F^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\), while \(\operatorname{dist}(0,F(x))=0\) for every \(x\). Hence no finite \(\kappa\) gives \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(0))\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,F(x))\) locally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With nonclosed values, canonical distance can vanish away from the true solution set, precluding a local error bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F^{-1}(0)=\{0\},\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,F(x))=0\ \forall x,\qquad \text{no finite local error-bound modulus exists.}\]
knowledge_statements.title: Failure under Nonclosed Residual Values

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full Solution Set Cannot Be Replaced by a Reference Singleton
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replacing the full inverse image by one solution changes ordinary subregularity into an isolated-solution property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=\{0\}\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R\), with \((\bar x,\bar y)=(0,0)\). Since \(F^{-1}(0)=\mathbb R\), the ordinary subregularity estimate holds trivially. The singleton estimate \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\{0\})\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,F(x))\) fails for every \(x\ne0\) and every finite \(\kappa\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Control of distance to the full solution set does not imply control of distance to a chosen reference solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(0))=0,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(x,\{0\})\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,F(x))\text{ fails locally.}\]
knowledge_statements.title: Full Solution Set Cannot Be Replaced by a Reference Singleton

assumptions_latex: Use the alternative residual \(\rho(x)=x^2\), which has the same zero set as \(r(x)=|x|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[|x|\le\kappa r(x)\text{ holds with }\kappa=1,\qquad |x|\le c\rho(x)\text{ fails locally for every finite }c.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit scalar counterexample is directly checkable
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic flattening destroys equivalence despite preserving the zero set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Here \(S=F^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\) and \(r(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,F(x))=|x|\), so
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)=|x|\le r(x).\]
For \(\rho(x)=x^2\), a local Lipschitz error bound would require \(|x|\le c x^2\) for all sufficiently small \(x\). For every finite \(c\), this fails whenever \(0<|x|<1/c\). Thus preservation of the solution set without a positive local lower comparison to the canonical residual does not preserve the correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing the canonical residual |x| by x squared preserves its zero set but destroys every local Lipschitz error bound at zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Equivalence Failure Boundaries

children.title: Constraint-Qualification Routes
children.top_down_role: Error-bound criteria derived from regularity of nonlinear constraint systems.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal-Transversality Route to a Feasibility Error Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth preimage constraint system with a locally closed target and limiting-normal transversality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\), let \(D\subset\mathbb R^m\) be locally closed near \(g(\bar x)\), and suppose \(g(\bar x)\in D\). Define \(M(x):=g(x)-D\) and \(\Omega:=\{x:g(x)\in D\}\). If
\[
\lambda\in N_D(g(\bar x)),\quad \nabla g(\bar x)^T\lambda=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \lambda=0,
\]
where \(N_D\) is the limiting normal cone, then \(M\) is metrically regular at \((\bar x,0)\). Consequently, some neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(\kappa<\infty\) satisfy
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,\Omega)\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(g(x),D)\qquad(x\in U).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exclusion of nonzero target normals annihilated by the constraint Jacobian yields metric regularity of the constraint mapping and a local feasibility error bound.
assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
\(D\subset\mathbb R^m\) is locally closed near \(g(\bar x)\), and \(g(\bar x)\in D\).
For the limiting normal cone, \(\nabla g(\bar x)^T\lambda=0\) and \(\lambda\in N_D(g(\bar x))\) imply \(\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(x)=g(x)-D\) is metrically regular at \((\bar x,0)\), and locally \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\Omega)\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(g(x),D)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Transversality Route to a Feasibility Error Bound

assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is continuously differentiable, \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^m\) is closed, and \(g(\bar x)\in D\).
The transversality condition \(\nabla g(\bar x)^T\lambda=0\), \(\lambda\in N_D(g(\bar x))\) implies \(\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{dist}(x,\{u:g(u)\in D\})\le\kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(g(x),D)\quad(x\in U).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional transversality route from a constraint qualification to an error bound.

source_refs.locator: 4.2.2 Pointbased Characterizations of Covering and Metric Regularity p. 394
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the stated transversality condition, the constraint mapping \(M(x)=g(x)-D\) is metrically regular near \((\bar x,0)\), hence metrically subregular there. Consequently, there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(\kappa\ge0\) such that
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,\Omega)\le\kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(0,M(x))=\kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(g(x),D)\quad\text{for every }x\in U,\]
where \(\Omega=\{x:g(x)\in D\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normal-cone transversality constraint qualification yields metric regularity of the constraint mapping and therefore a local feasibility error bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Qualification Routes

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose there exist \(\delta>0\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and \(\tau>0\) such that
\[
 |\nabla f|(x)\ge \tau
 \quad\text{whenever}\quad
 d(x,\bar x)<\delta\ \text{ and }\ 0<f(x)<\varepsilon.
\]
Then, after possibly reducing \(\delta\), every \(x\) with \(d(x,\bar x)<\delta\) satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le \frac{[f(x)]_+}{\tau}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform positive lower bound on the strong slope at nearby infeasible points yields a local error bound with reciprocal modulus.
knowledge_statements.title: Slope Criteria

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Necessity of a Strong-Slope Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative converse to strong-slope sufficiency in the convex scalar setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on a normed space, let \(S:=\{x:f(x)\le0\}\neq\varnothing\), and suppose \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa[f(x)]_+\] on a convex neighborhood of \(\bar x\in S\). After shrinking the neighborhood if necessary, \[|\nabla f|(x)\ge\kappa^{-1}\] at every included point with \(f(x)>0\). Thus local linear error bounds and uniform positive strong-slope bounds are quantitatively equivalent in this convex regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex function, a local error bound forces the reciprocal lower bound on strong slope.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on a normed space.
A local error bound with modulus \(\kappa\) holds on a convex neighborhood of \(\bar x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\nabla f|(x)\ge1/\kappa\) at nearby points with \(f(x)>0\).

notation.meaning: strong slope of the convex function

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If there exist \(\delta>0\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and \(\tau>0\) such that
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge\tau
 \quad\text{for all }x\text{ with }
 \|x-\bar x\|<\delta\text{ and }0<f(x)<\varepsilon,
\]
then, after shrinking the neighborhood if necessary,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le \tau^{-1}[f(x)]_+.
\]
Thus the displayed subgradient separation is a dual certificate of the error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex function, uniformly separating zero from nearby infeasible subdifferentials certifies a local error bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Subdifferential Criteria

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2.2 Pointbased Characterizations of Covering and Metric Regularity p. 394
