\(f\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to a \(C^2\) manifold \(M\), with \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_k\to\bar v\) and \(v_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) need not imply \(x_k\in M\) eventually when \(\bar v\notin\operatorname{ri}\partial f(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Limiting subdifferential of the extended-real-valued function.
Active manifold relative to which partial smoothness holds.
Relative interior of a convex set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary created by loss of the relative-interior nondegeneracy condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partial smoothness alone does not guarantee identification. Let \(x_k\to\bar x\), let \(f(x_k)\to f(\bar x)\), and choose \(v_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) with \(v_k\to\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\). Standard identification results require a compatibility condition such as \(\bar v\in\operatorname{ri}\partial f(\bar x)\). If this condition fails, the graph of \(\partial f\) may contain sequences approaching \((\bar x,\bar v)\) from strata other than \(M\); consequently, eventual membership \(x_k\in M\) cannot in general be inferred.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without relative-interior nondegeneracy, subgradient pairs can converge to the reference pair while their primal points repeatedly remain outside the active manifold.
knowledge_statements.title: Compatibility Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the asserted necessity of relative-interior nondegeneracy requires an identification theorem and an explicit counterexample or authoritative failure result.

children.title: Finite Active-Manifold Identification
children.top_down_role: Finite discovery of active geometric structure by convergent method families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-step proximal-gradient specialization of convex graph-pair identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=h+g\), where \(h\) is \(C^1\) with locally Lipschitz gradient and \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and partly smooth at \( ar x\) relative to \(M\). Suppose, for fixed \(\gamma>0\), \[x_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(x_k-\gamma
abla h(x_k)),\qquad x_k	o ar x,\] and \(-
abla h( ar x)\in\operatorname{ri}\partial g( ar x)\). Defining \[v_{k+1}=\gamma^{-1}(x_k-x_{k+1})-
abla h(x_k),\] one has \(v_{k+1}\in\partial g(x_{k+1})\), \(v_{k+1}	o-
abla h( ar x)\), and \(x_k\in M\) eventually.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convergent proximal-gradient sequence finitely identifies the partly smooth manifold, and its proximal optimality residual supplies the required subgradient graph pairs.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to \(M\).
The fixed-step proximal-gradient sequence converges to \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{k+1}\in\partial g(x_{k+1}),\quad v_{k+1}\to-\nabla h(\bar x),\quad \exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ x_k\in M.\)

notation.meaning: proximal mapping of the scaled function
subgradient reconstructed from the proximal-gradient step

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Identification by Proximal Gradient

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex partly smooth functions and convergent subgradient graph pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to a \(C^2\) manifold \(M\). If \((x_k,v_k)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\), \((x_k,v_k)\to(\bar x,\bar v)\), and \(\bar v\in\operatorname{ri}\partial f(\bar x)\), then \[\exists K\in\mathbb N\;\forall k\ge K:\quad x_k\in M.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergent subgradient graph pairs identify a convex partly smooth active manifold finitely when the limiting subgradient is relatively interior.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ x_k\in M.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Graph-Pair Identification Theorem

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to a \(C^2\) manifold \(M\).
\(x_k\to\bar x\), \(f(x_k)\to f(\bar x)\), and \(v_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) satisfy \(v_k\to\bar v\in\operatorname{ri}\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\in\mathbb{N}\;\forall k\ge K:\ x_k\in M\).

notation.meaning: Active manifold of the partly smooth function.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequence-form finite identification theorem for partly smooth functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the stated partial-smoothness and nondegeneracy hypotheses, the active manifold is identifiable from convergent subgradient pairs: there exists \(K\in\mathbb{N}\) such that \(x_k\in M\) for every \(k\ge K\). Thus any convergent method producing pairs \((x_k,v_k)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\), with function-value convergence and dual limit in \(\operatorname{ri}\partial f(\bar x)\), discovers the active geometric structure after finitely many iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convergent method whose limiting subgradient is nondegenerate enters the partly smooth active manifold after finitely many iterations.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Active-Manifold Identification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits finite identification, but for a nonconvex limiting-subdifferential formulation the exact partial-smoothness, prox-regularity, and subdifferential-continuity hypotheses must be checked against a specific identification theorem.

children.title: Post-Identification Smooth Reduction
children.top_down_role: Transition from nonsmooth iterations to smooth local manifold models.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Identification Does Not Imply a Quadratic Newton Phase
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar smooth reduced problem showing the need for reduced-Hessian regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take \(M=\mathbb R\), \(f|_M(x)=x^4\), and \(\bar x=0\). The manifold is already identified, but \(\nabla_M^2 f(0)=0\). For \(x_k\ne0\), Newton's update is \[x_{k+1}=x_k-\frac{4x_k^3}{12x_k^2}=\frac23x_k,\] so convergence is linear rather than quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the reduced objective x to the fourth power, identification is immediate but singular curvature leaves Newton's method only linearly convergent.
assumptions_latex: \(M=\mathbb R\), \(f(x)=x^4\), and \(x_0\ne0\) is sufficiently near zero.
Classical Newton steps are applied to the reduced stationarity equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=\frac23x_k\), so the convergence to \(0\) is linear and not quadratic.
knowledge_statements.title: Identification Does Not Imply a Quadratic Newton Phase

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduction of late iterates to the smooth restriction, without asserting equivalence to unconstrained nonsmooth stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be partly smooth relative to a \(C^2\) manifold \(M\), and suppose \(x_k\in M\) for all sufficiently large \(k\). If \(f|_M\) is \(C^2\), then the late-iterate objective is the smooth manifold function \(f|_M\); its intrinsic first- and second-order models are \(
abla_M(f|_M)\) and \(
abla_M^2(f|_M)\). Stationarity of the reduced problem is therefore \(
abla_M(f|_M)(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After finite identification, late iterates can be modeled by the smooth restriction of the objective to the active manifold.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is partly smooth relative to a \(C^2\) manifold \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_k)=(f|_M)(x_k)\text{ eventually, with reduced stationarity }\nabla_M(f|_M)(x)=0.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Restricted Model after Identification

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Riemannian Newton Convergence after Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Newton theorem for the smooth restricted problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the iterates have identified a smooth active manifold \(M\), \( ar x\) satisfies \(
abla_M(f|_M)( ar x)=0\), and \(f|_M\) has a locally Lipschitz Riemannian Hessian near \( ar x\). If \(
abla_M^2(f|_M)( ar x):T_M( ar x)	o T_M( ar x)\) is invertible, then the Riemannian Newton iteration \[
abla_M^2(f|_M)(x_k)[s_k]=-
abla_M(f|_M)(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(s_k),\] with a second-order retraction \(R\), is locally well defined and converges quadratically to \( ar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible, locally Lipschitz reduced Hessian yields a quadratic Newton phase on the identified manifold.
assumptions_latex: The iterates eventually lie on the active manifold \(M\).
The Riemannian Hessian is locally Lipschitz and invertible at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}_M(x_{k+1},\bar x)\le C\operatorname{dist}_M(x_k,\bar x)^2\text{ for all sufficiently large }k.\)

notation.meaning: retraction from the tangent space to the manifold

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Riemannian Newton Convergence after Identification

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is partly smooth relative to a \(C^2\) manifold \(M\) near a critical point \(\bar x\).
An iterative method identifies \(M\): \(x_k\in M\) for every sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)=f|_M(x)\) for \(x\in M\), and post-identification derivatives are the Riemannian derivatives \(\nabla_M f(x)\) and \(\nabla_M^2 f(x)\) whenever the latter exists.

notation.meaning: Restriction of the objective to the active manifold.
Riemannian gradient on the active manifold.
Riemannian Hessian on the active manifold.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local manifold reduction after finite active-set identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Once \(M\) is identified, all sufficiently late iterates lie in a neighborhood where the active restriction \(f|_M\) is smooth. The original nonsmooth local model can therefore be replaced along feasible tangent directions by the Riemannian model on \(M\). In particular, first-order stationarity reduces to \(\nabla_M f(x)=0\), and, when \(f|_M\) is twice differentiable, local Newton or quasi-Newton steps may be formulated using \(\nabla_M^2 f(x)\) on \(T_M(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After identification, the nonsmooth problem locally becomes a smooth optimization problem on the active manifold.
knowledge_statements.title: Post-Identification Smooth Reduction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the leaf, but identification alone does not justify every claimed Newton or quasi-Newton reduction. A source must specify the smoothness and algorithmic hypotheses under which the Riemannian model replaces the nonsmooth model.

children.title: Tame Desingularization-Error-Bound Interface
children.top_down_role: The interface between definable geometry, desingularization, local error bounds, and descent convergence.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Section 8.4.2: Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz theory

children.title: Definable Geometry Regime Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Tame object classes supporting desingularization and stratification.

children.title: Semialgebraic Regimes
children.top_down_role: Semialgebraic object classes supporting tame local geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finiteness and path structure of semialgebraic connected components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every semialgebraic set has finitely many connected components. Each component is semialgebraic, and every connected semialgebraic set is semialgebraically path connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semialgebraic sets have finitely many semialgebraic connected components, each admitting semialgebraic paths.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^N S_i\text{ for finitely many semialgebraic connected components }S_i,\text{ each semialgebraically path connected}.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Semialgebraic Component Structure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection closure and quantifier elimination for real semialgebraic sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+m}\) is semialgebraic, then its coordinate projection \(\pi(S)\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is semialgebraic. Equivalently, every first-order formula over the real closed field using polynomial equalities and inequalities is equivalent over \(\mathbb R\) to a quantifier-free formula of that form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate projections of semialgebraic sets are semialgebraic; equivalently, real polynomial formulas admit quantifier elimination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \pi(S)\text{ is semialgebraic}.

notation.meaning: Coordinate projection onto the first n coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Tarski–Seidenberg Projection Theorem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite smooth stratification compatible with a prescribed finite semialgebraic family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every finite family of semialgebraic subsets of \(\mathbb R^n\) admits a finite compatible semialgebraic Whitney \((a)\) stratification; in particular, each set is a union of smooth semialgebraic strata satisfying the frontier condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite semialgebraic families admit compatible finite smooth Whitney stratifications.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ a finite compatible semialgebraic Whitney }(a)\text{ stratification satisfying the frontier condition}.
knowledge_statements.title: Semialgebraic Whitney Stratification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semialgebraic-arc representation of closure points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is semialgebraic and \(\bar x\in\overline S\setminus S\), then there exist \(\varepsilon>0\) and a continuous semialgebraic curve \(\gamma:[0,\varepsilon)\to\mathbb R^n\) such that \(\gamma(0)=\bar x\) and \(\gamma(t)\in S\) for every \(t\in(0,\varepsilon)\). The curve may be chosen real analytic on \((0,\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every boundary approach to a semialgebraic set can be witnessed by a semialgebraic arc.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\gamma\text{ semialgebraic with }\gamma(0)=\bar x\text{ and }\gamma((0,\varepsilon))\subseteq S.
knowledge_statements.title: Semialgebraic Curve Selection

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is semialgebraic exactly when it is a finite union of sets described by finitely many polynomial equalities and strict inequalities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical finite-dimensional semialgebraic category.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The set \(S\) is semialgebraic if there exist finite index sets and real polynomials \(p_{ij},q_{ij}\in\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) such that
\[
S=\bigcup_{i=1}^{r}\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n: p_{ij}(x)=0\ \text{for all }j,\ q_{i\ell}(x)>0\ \text{for all }\ell\right\}.
\]
A function \(f:S\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is semialgebraic when its graph \(\{(x,f(x)):x\in S\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+m}\) is semialgebraic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semialgebraic sets are finite unions of solution sets of finite polynomial equality and inequality systems; semialgebraic functions have semialgebraic graphs.
knowledge_statements.title: Semialgebraic Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is standard, mathematically precise, and appropriately placed, but no inspectable citation with a section, definition, or page locator is supplied.

children.title: Definable Regimes
children.top_down_role: Object classes definable within an o-minimal structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic dimension identities for sets and mappings definable in one o-minimal structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For definable sets \(A,B\), \(\dim(A\cup B)=\max\{\dim A,\dim B\}\). For a definable mapping \(f:A\to\mathbb R^m\), \(\dim f(A)\le\dim A\); equality holds if \(f\) is injective, and definable bijections preserve dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Definable dimension is stable under finite unions, cannot increase under definable images, and is invariant under definable bijections.
assumptions_latex: A,B\text{ and }\operatorname{gph}f\text{ are definable in one fixed o-minimal structure}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \dim(A\cup B)=\max\{\dim A,\dim B\},\qquad \dim f(A)\le\dim A.
knowledge_statements.title: Definable Dimension Calculus

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection theorem for a definable family of nonempty fibers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A\subseteq\mathbb R^{m+n}\) is definable, then there exists a definable mapping \(s:\pi(A)\to\mathbb R^n\) such that \((x,s(x))\in A\) for every \(x\in\pi(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A definable family of nonempty fibers admits a definable selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists s:\pi(A)\to\mathbb R^n\text{ definable such that }s(x)\in A_x\text{ for every }x\in\pi(A).
knowledge_statements.title: Definable Choice

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definable-arc representation of closure points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is definable and \(\bar x\in\overline A\setminus A\), then there exist \(\varepsilon>0\) and a continuous definable curve \(\gamma:[0,\varepsilon)\to\mathbb R^n\) such that \(\gamma(0)=\bar x\) and \(\gamma(t)\in A\) for every \(t\in(0,\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every closure point of a definable set can be approached along a definable curve lying in the set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\gamma\text{ continuous and definable with }\gamma(0)=\bar x\text{ and }\gamma((0,\varepsilon))\subseteq A.
knowledge_statements.title: Definable Curve Selection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite one-dimensional regularity decomposition for definable functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f:(a,b)\to\mathbb R\) is definable, then there is a finite partition \(a=t_0<\cdots<t_N=b\) such that on every \((t_{i-1},t_i)\), the function \(f\) is continuous and either constant or strictly monotone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-variable definable function is piecewise continuous and either constant or strictly monotone on finitely many intervals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists a=t_0<\cdots<t_N=b\text{ with the stated continuity and monotonicity property on each }(t_{i-1},t_i).
knowledge_statements.title: Definable Monotonicity Theorem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite cell decomposition compatible with a prescribed finite family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every finite family \(A_1,\ldots,A_r\) of definable subsets of \(\mathbb R^n\), there exists a finite definable cell decomposition of \(\mathbb R^n\) compatible with every \(A_i\); each \(A_i\) is a union of cells of the decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite family of definable sets admits one compatible finite definable cell decomposition.
assumptions_latex: A_1,\ldots,A_r\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ are definable in one fixed o-minimal structure}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ a finite definable cell decomposition of }\mathbb R^n\text{ compatible with every }A_i.
knowledge_statements.title: Definable Cell Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite smooth stratification compatible with prescribed definable subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_1,\ldots,A_r\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be definable and let \(p\ge1\). There exists a finite definable \(C^p\) stratification of \(\mathbb R^n\) compatible with every \(A_i\); it may be chosen to satisfy the frontier condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite family of definable sets admits a compatible finite smooth definable stratification.
assumptions_latex: A_1,\ldots,A_r\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ are definable in one fixed o-minimal structure}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ a finite compatible definable }C^p\text{ stratification satisfying the frontier condition}.
knowledge_statements.title: Definable Smooth Stratification

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{R}=(\mathcal{R}_n)_{n\ge1}\) is a fixed o-minimal structure over the ordered real field.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is definable when \(S\in\mathcal{R}_n\), and \(f:S\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is definable when \(\operatorname{gph}f\in\mathcal{R}_{n+m}\).

notation.meaning: Fixed o-minimal structure on the real field.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definability relative to one fixed o-minimal structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is definable in \(\mathcal R\) when \(S\in\mathcal R_n\). A mapping \(f:S\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is definable when its graph \(\operatorname{gph}f=\{(x,f(x)):x\in S\}\) belongs to \(\mathcal R_{n+m}\). The structure is closed under finite Boolean operations, Cartesian products, and coordinate projections, while o-minimality requires every member of \(\mathcal R_1\) to be a finite union of points and open intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set or function is definable when it belongs, or has a graph belonging, to a fixed o-minimal structure.
knowledge_statements.title: Definable Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly fixes one o-minimal structure and defines mappings through their graphs, but it lacks the required inspectable citation.

children.title: O-Minimal Expansion Regimes
children.top_down_role: Broader tame settings obtained through expansions of definable structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Growth boundary separating two standard o-minimal expansion regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The structure \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{an}}\) is polynomially bounded: for every definable \(f:(a,+\infty)\to\mathbb R\), there is \(N\in\mathbb N\) such that \(|f(x)|\le x^N\) for all sufficiently large \(x\). The expansion \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{an},\exp}\) is not polynomially bounded because the global exponential function is definable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricted-analytic geometry is polynomially bounded, whereas adjoining the global exponential crosses that growth boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb R_{\mathrm{an}}\text{ is polynomially bounded, whereas }\mathbb R_{\mathrm{an},\exp}\text{ is not}.

notation.meaning: Expansion of the ordered real field by all restricted real-analytic functions.
Further expansion by the global exponential function.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomially Bounded Versus Exponential Expansions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard proper o-minimal expansions of the semialgebraic structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) denote the semialgebraic structure, \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{an}}\) the expansion by all restricted real-analytic functions, and \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{an},\exp}\) the further expansion by the global exponential function. These structures are o-minimal and satisfy \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\subsetneq\mathbb R_{\mathrm{an}}\subsetneq\mathbb R_{\mathrm{an},\exp}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricted analytic functions and then the global exponential give proper classical o-minimal expansions of the semialgebraic structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\subsetneq\mathbb R_{\mathrm{an}}\subsetneq\mathbb R_{\mathrm{an},\exp},\qquad\text{and all three structures are o-minimal}.

notation.meaning: Expansion by restricted real-analytic functions and global exponential.

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Analytic–Exponential Expansion Hierarchy
O-Minimal Expansion Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested o-minimal structures and preservation of objects definable in the base structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R=(\mathcal R_n)_{n\ge 1}\) and \(\mathcal S=(\mathcal S_n)_{n\ge 1}\) be o-minimal structures over the ordered real field. The structure \(\mathcal S\) is an expansion of \(\mathcal R\) when \(\mathcal R_n\subseteq\mathcal S_n\) for every \(n\ge 1\). Consequently, every set definable in \(\mathcal R\), and every mapping whose graph is definable in \(\mathcal R\), is also definable in \(\mathcal S\); the converse need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An o-minimal expansion contains every set and mapping definable in the base structure and may contain additional definable objects.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal R=(\mathcal R_n)_{n\ge1}\) and \(\mathcal S=(\mathcal S_n)_{n\ge1}\) are o-minimal structures over the ordered real field.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal S\) expands \(\mathcal R\) exactly when \(\mathcal R_n\subseteq\mathcal S_n\) for every \(n\ge1\); every \(\mathcal R\)-definable object is then \(\mathcal S\)-definable.

children.title: Definability Transfer Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on transferring tame conclusions across definability classes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure of closure under externally indexed countable constructions in any o-minimal expansion of the ordered real field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Enumerate \(\mathbb Q=\{q_1,q_2,\ldots\}\), set \(S_n=\{q_1,\ldots,q_n\}\), and let \(g_n=\mathbf 1_{S_n}\). Every \(S_n\) and \(g_n\) is semialgebraic and hence definable in every expansion of the ordered real field. Nevertheless, \(\bigcup_nS_n=\mathbb Q\) and \(g_n\to\mathbf 1_{\mathbb Q}\) pointwise, while neither \(\mathbb Q\) nor \(\mathbf 1_{\mathbb Q}\) is definable in an o-minimal structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite definable sets can have a nondefinable countable union, and their indicator functions can converge pointwise to a nondefinable function.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal R\text{ is an o-minimal expansion of the ordered real field}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_n\text{ and }g_n\text{ are }\mathcal R\text{-definable, whereas }\mathbb Q\text{ and }\mathbf 1_{\mathbb Q}\text{ are not}.

notation.meaning: The function equal to one on S and zero outside S.

knowledge_statements.title: Countable-Union and Pointwise-Limit Failure

assumptions_latex: \(f:A\to\mathbb{R}^m\) and the parameter set \(A\) are definable in one fixed o-minimal structure \(\mathcal R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Definability transfers through operations expressible by finite Boolean combinations, Cartesian products, coordinate projections, and definable compositions, but not through unrestricted countable unions, arbitrary limits, or quantification over \(\mathbb N\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure boundary for transferring definability through constructions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Definability is preserved by finite unions and intersections, complements, Cartesian products, coordinate projections, and compositions of definable mappings. Consequently, sets described by first-order formulas over \(\mathcal R\) with finitely many real quantifiers remain definable. No analogous closure holds for unrestricted countable operations: a countable union of definable sets, a pointwise limit of definable functions, or a construction encoding arbitrary quantification over \(\mathbb N\) need not be definable. Transfer claims must therefore exhibit a finite definable construction in one common structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite first-order constructions preserve definability; arbitrary countable unions, limits, and integer-indexed constructions generally do not.
knowledge_statements.title: Definability Transfer Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-construction closure boundary is broadly correct and fits the leaf, but the claims about pointwise limits and unrestricted integer-indexed constructions require an authoritative source or explicit counterexamples.

children.title: Whitney-Stratified Regimes
children.top_down_role: Smooth stratified structures relevant to local regularity and critical geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit separation of the frontier condition from Whitney secant regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[X=\{(x,x\sin(1/x)):x>0\},\qquad Y=\{(0,0)\},\qquad S=X\cup Y.\] The two-stratum partition \(S=X\sqcup Y\) is locally finite, consists of connected smooth embedded manifolds, and satisfies the frontier condition. Nevertheless, the incident pair \((X,Y)\) fails Whitney condition \((b)\) at the origin because limiting secant lines need not lie in the corresponding limiting tangent lines.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oscillatory smooth curve and its endpoint satisfy the frontier condition but fail Whitney secant compatibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S=X\sqcup Y\text{ satisfies the frontier condition but }(X,Y)\text{ fails Whitney }(b)\text{ at }0.
knowledge_statements.title: Frontier-Compatible Stratification Failing Whitney (b)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical relation between the two incidence conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an incident pair of \(C^1\) strata \((X,Y)\), Whitney condition \((b)\) at \(y\in Y\) implies Whitney condition \((a)\) at \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whitney secant compatibility implies the weaker limiting-tangent compatibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (X,Y)\text{ satisfies Whitney }(a)\text{ at }y.
knowledge_statements.title: Whitney (b) Implies Whitney (a)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence of Compatible Whitney Stratifications for Subanalytic Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional existence theorem in the subanalytic category.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every subanalytic subset of \(\mathbb R^n\) admits a locally finite Whitney \((b)\) stratification by connected real-analytic submanifolds. The stratification may be chosen compatible with a prescribed locally finite family of subanalytic subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subanalytic sets admit compatible Whitney stratifications by analytic strata.
assumptions_latex: \{S_j\}\text{ is a prescribed locally finite subanalytic family when compatibility is required}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ admits a locally finite Whitney }(b)\text{ stratification compatible with each }S_j.
knowledge_statements.title: Existence of Compatible Whitney Stratifications for Subanalytic Sets
Whitney-Stratified Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional locally finite stratifications satisfying the frontier and Whitney conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A locally finite partition of \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) into connected embedded \(C^1\) submanifolds is a Whitney stratification if it satisfies the frontier condition and every incident pair of strata satisfies Whitney conditions \((a)\) and \((b)\). The frontier condition requires that if strata \(X\) and \(Y\) satisfy \(Y\cap\overline X\ne\varnothing\), then \(Y\subseteq\overline X\). For \(y\in Y\subseteq\overline X\), condition \((a)\) requires \(T_yY\subseteq T\) whenever \(x_k\in X\), \(x_k\to y\), and \(T_{x_k}X\to T\). Condition \((b)\) requires \(L\subseteq T\) whenever additionally \(y_k\in Y\), \(y_k\to y\), \(x_k\ne y_k\), and the secant lines \(\mathbb R(x_k-y_k)\) converge to \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Whitney stratification is a locally finite smooth partition satisfying the frontier condition and compatibility of limiting tangent spaces and secant lines for every incident pair of strata.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is partitioned into locally finite, connected, embedded \(C^1\) submanifolds called strata.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partition is Whitney stratified when it satisfies the frontier condition and every incident pair of strata satisfies Whitney conditions \((a)\) and \((b)\).

notation.meaning: Incident stratum contained in the closure of X.
Tangent space to X at x.

children.title: Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz Principle
children.top_down_role: The desingularization family connecting tame geometry, slopes, and local error bounds.

children.title: Łojasiewicz Gradient Regime
children.top_down_role: Analytic and smooth antecedents of the general desingularization principle.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Smooth Flat Function Without a Power Gradient Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit boundary showing that arbitrary smoothness cannot replace analyticity in the classical theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(f(0)=0\) and \(f(x)=e^{-1/x^2}\) for \(x\ne0\). Then \(f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R)\) and \(f'(0)=0\), but for every \(c>0\) and \(\theta\in[0,1)\), the inequality \(|f'(x)|\ge c|f(x)-f(0)|^\theta\) fails arbitrarily near \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard smooth flat function has no power-type Łojasiewicz gradient inequality at its critical point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lim_{x\to0,\,x\ne0}\frac{|f'(x)|}{|f(x)|^\theta}=0,\quad\text{so no positive local gradient-inequality constant exists}.
knowledge_statements.title: A Smooth Flat Function Without a Power Gradient Inequality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Length of Convergent Analytic Gradient Trajectories
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical trajectory consequence of the analytic gradient inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be real analytic near \(\bar x\), and let \(x:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^n\) solve \(\dot x(t)=-\nabla f(x(t))\). If \(x(t)\to\bar x\), then \[\int_0^\infty\|\dot x(t)\|\,dt<\infty.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convergent trajectory of an analytic gradient flow has finite length.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is real analytic near the trajectory tail}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \int_0^\infty\|\dot x(t)\|\,dt<\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Length of Convergent Analytic Gradient Trajectories

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is real analytic near a critical point \(\bar x\), with \(\nabla f(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists c>0,\ \theta\in[0,1),\ \varepsilon>0\) such that \(\|\nabla f(x)\|\ge c|f(x)-f(\bar x)|^\theta\) whenever \(\|x-\bar x\|<\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean gradient of the analytic function.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical finite-dimensional analytic gradient inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exist constants \(c>0\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and \(\theta\in[0,1)\) such that
\[
\|\nabla f(x)\|\ge c\,|f(x)-f(\bar x)|^\theta
\]
for every \(x\) satisfying \(\|x-\bar x\|<\varepsilon\). Equivalently, with \(\varphi(s)=\frac{1}{c(1-\theta)}s^{1-\theta}\), one has \(\varphi'(|f(x)-f(\bar x)|)\|\nabla f(x)\|\ge1\) whenever the function-value gap is nonzero and sufficiently small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near an analytic critical point, the gradient norm controls a positive power of the function-value gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Łojasiewicz Gradient Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The analytic gradient inequality and its desingularized reformulation are consistent and fit the theorem container, but no specific authoritative locator is supplied.

children.title: Nonsmooth Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz Regime
children.top_down_role: Subdifferential desingularization for nonsmooth functions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Definable Functions Satisfy the Nonsmooth KL Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tame-geometric sufficient regime for the limiting-subdifferential KL property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and definable in an o-minimal structure. Then \(f\) has the limiting-subdifferential Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz property at every \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every proper lower-semicontinuous definable function satisfies the nonsmooth KL property at each point in its subdifferential domain.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and definable in one o-minimal structure}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ has the limiting-subdifferential KL property at }\bar x.
knowledge_statements.title: Definable Functions Satisfy the Nonsmooth KL Property

assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\), and \(\varphi:[0,\eta)\to\mathbb{R}_+\) is continuous, concave, \(C^1\) on \((0,\eta)\), with \(\varphi(0)=0\) and \(\varphi'>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1\) on a punctured local upper level set.

notation.meaning: Effective domain of the limiting subdifferential.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting-subdifferential form of the local KL property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(f\) has the Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz property at \(\bar x\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\), a number \(\eta>0\), and a desingularizing function \(\varphi\) as specified above such that
\[
\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1
\]
for every \(x\in U\) satisfying \(f(\bar x)<f(x)<f(\bar x)+\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonsmooth KL property bounds the reciprocal subgradient slope by the derivative of a concave desingularizing function.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The limiting-subdifferential KL condition is standard, internally consistent, and correctly classified as a condition, but it lacks a citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Uniformized Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz Regime
children.top_down_role: Uniform desingularization near compact critical sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact constant-level uniformization when all pointwise KL inequalities have power form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) be compact, let \(f\equiv f_\Omega\) on \(\Omega\), and suppose that for every \(z\in\Omega\) there are local constants \(c_z,\eta_z>0\) and an exponent \(\theta_z\in[0,1)\) such that \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge c_z(f(x)-f_\Omega)^{\theta_z}\) near \(z\) whenever \(0<f(x)-f_\Omega<\eta_z\). Then there exist \(c,\varepsilon,\eta>0\) and \(\theta\in[0,1)\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge c(f(x)-f_\Omega)^\theta\] whenever \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\Omega)<\varepsilon\) and \(0<f(x)-f_\Omega<\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise power-type KL inequalities on a compact constant-value set admit one common exponent and common local constants.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ has a local power-type KL inequality at every }z\in\Omega.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists c,\varepsilon,\eta>0,\ \theta\in[0,1)\text{ giving one uniform power-type KL inequality near }\Omega.

notation.meaning: Common value of f on the compact set Omega.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniformization of Power-Type KL Exponents

assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subseteq\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) is compact, \(f\) is constant on \(\Omega\), and \(f\) has the KL property at every point of \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One neighborhood, one positive height, and one desingularizing function give the KL inequality uniformly near \(\Omega\).

notation.meaning: Compact set on which the function has one value.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniformization of pointwise KL inequalities over a compact level set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exist \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\eta>0\), and a single admissible concave function \(\varphi:[0,\eta)\to\mathbb{R}_+\) such that, for every \(\bar x\in\Omega\) and every \(x\) satisfying \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\Omega)<\varepsilon\) and \(f(\bar x)<f(x)<f(\bar x)+\eta\),
\[
\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1.
\]
Because \(f\) is constant on \(\Omega\), the reference value is independent of the selected \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise KL inequalities on a compact constant-value set can be replaced by one inequality with common neighborhood, height, and desingularizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniformized Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The compact constant-value uniformization theorem is appropriately placed and plausibly stated, but its common desingularizer conclusion requires a specific theorem citation.

children.title: Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz Exponent Regimes
children.top_down_role: Qualitative local rate regimes indexed by desingularization geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponent convention for the limiting-subdifferential KL inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proper lower-semicontinuous function \(f\) has the KL property at \(\bar x\) with exponent \(\theta\in[0,1)\) if there exist \(c,\eta>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge c\bigl(f(x)-f(\bar x)\bigr)^\theta\] whenever \(x\in U\) and \(0<f(x)-f(\bar x)<\eta\). Equivalently, the KL inequality admits a desingularizer proportional to \(s^{1-\theta}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A KL exponent is the power governing the local lower bound on subgradient size in terms of objective gap.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper and lower semicontinuous}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge c(f(x)-f(\bar x))^\theta\text{ locally whenever }0<f(x)-f(\bar x)<\eta.
knowledge_statements.title: Power-Type KL Exponent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness of admissible power exponents and the exponent-threshold convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the local KL inequality holds with exponent \(\theta\in[0,1)\), then, after restricting the objective gap to be less than one, it also holds with every \(\theta'\in[\theta,1)\). Consequently, the informative invariant is the infimum of the admissible exponents, whether or not that infimum is itself attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Larger KL exponents give weaker local inequalities, so the informative exponent is the admissible threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\theta'\in[\theta,1):\quad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge c(f(x)-f(\bar x))^{\theta'}.
knowledge_statements.title: Admissible-Exponent Monotonicity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-gap rates for the scalar recursion induced by power-type KL geometry; no iterate-distance rate is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((r_k)\subset[0,\infty)\) be nonincreasing with \(r_k\to0\), and suppose that for some \(\mu>0\), \(k_0\), and \(\theta\in[0,1)\), \[r_{k-1}-r_k\ge \mu r_k^{2\theta}\qquad(k\ge k_0).\] If \(\theta=0\), then \(r_k=0\) after finitely many steps. If \(0<\theta\le\tfrac12\), then \(r_k\le Cq^k\) eventually for some \(C>0\) and \(q\in(0,1)\). If \(\tfrac12<\theta<1\), then \(r_k=O(k^{-1/(2\theta-1)})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard KL gap recursion gives finite termination, geometric gap decay, or polynomial gap decay according to the exponent.
assumptions_latex: r_{k-1}-r_k\ge\mu r_k^{2\theta}\text{ for all sufficiently large }k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \theta=0\Rightarrow\text{finite termination};\quad0<\theta\le\tfrac12\Rightarrow r_k=O(q^k);\quad\tfrac12<\theta<1\Rightarrow r_k=O(k^{-1/(2\theta-1)}).

notation.meaning: Nonnegative objective gap at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.title: Scalar KL-Gap Recursion Regimes

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KL Exponent Alone Does Not Determine a Sequence Rate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between function geometry and rates of sequences not linked to the function by descent estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The analytic function \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\) has KL exponent \(\tfrac12\) at \(0\), while the sequence \(x_k=(k+1)^{-1}\) converges to \(0\) only at rate \(\Theta(k^{-1})\). Thus the KL exponent alone does not imply the usual algorithmic rate trichotomy without descent and relative-error relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic KL function admits a slowly convergent arbitrary sequence, so algorithmic rates require relations between the sequence and the function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ has KL exponent }\tfrac12\text{ at }0,\qquad x_k\to0,\qquad |x_k|=\Theta(k^{-1}).
knowledge_statements.title: KL Exponent Alone Does Not Determine a Sequence Rate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Abstract KL Finite-Length and Iterate-Rate Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterate-distance trichotomy under explicit sufficient-decrease and relative-error assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_k\to\bar x\), let \(f(x_k)\to f(\bar x)\), and suppose that eventually
\[f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge a\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x_{k+1}))\le b\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\]
for \(a,b>0\). If \(f\) has KL exponent \(\theta\in[0,1)\) at \(\bar x\), then \(\sum_k\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|<\infty\). Moreover, \(\theta=0\) gives finite termination; \(0<\theta\le\tfrac12\) gives \(\|x_k-\bar x\|\le Cq^k\) eventually; and \(\tfrac12<\theta<1\) gives
\[\|x_k-\bar x\|=O\!\left(k^{-(1-\theta)/(2\theta-1)}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sufficient decrease and relative error convert a KL exponent into finite length and the standard finite, linear, or polynomial iterate-rate regimes.
assumptions_latex: The displayed sufficient-decrease and relative-error inequalities hold eventually with \(a,b>0\).
\(f\) has the power-type KL property at \(\bar x\) with exponent \(\theta\in[0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_k\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|<\infty\), with finite, linear, or \(O(k^{-(1-\theta)/(2\theta-1)})\) iterate convergence according to \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.title: Abstract KL Finite-Length and Iterate-Rate Theorem

assumptions_latex: A descent sequence \((x_k)\) converges to \(\bar x\) and satisfies standard sufficient-decrease and relative-error estimates near \(\bar x\).
The KL inequality holds with \(\varphi(s)=c s^{1-\theta}\), where \(c>0\) and \(\theta\in[0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta=0\) permits finite termination; \(0<\theta\le\tfrac12\) yields local linear convergence; \(\tfrac12<\theta<1\) yields a sublinear power rate.

notation.meaning: Limit point of the descent sequence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard qualitative rates for KL descent sequences; constants depend on algorithmic estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the stated descent assumptions, the exponent determines the qualitative local regime. If \(\theta=0\), the sequence terminates finitely at a critical point. If \(0<\theta\le\tfrac12\), there exist \(C>0\) and \(q\in(0,1)\) such that \(\|x_k-\bar x\|\le Cq^k\) for all sufficiently large \(k\). If \(\tfrac12<\theta<1\), the standard recursion yields \(\|x_k-\bar x\|=O(k^{-(1-\theta)/(2\theta-1)})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For standard KL descent methods, exponent zero permits finite termination, small positive exponents give linear convergence, and larger exponents give sublinear power rates.
knowledge_statements.title: Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz Exponent Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated iterate-rate trichotomy depends on precise sufficient-decrease, relative-error, and indexing hypotheses that are not given. Because it includes explicit convergence bounds, complexity_bound is more appropriate than property. A source is needed before a reliable replacement theorem can be formulated.

children.title: Tame Convergence of Descent Methods
children.top_down_role: Convergence families obtained by combining descent structure, stationarity control, and Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz geometry.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Section 8.4: sequential convergence under sufficient descent

children.title: Finite-Length Convergence
children.top_down_role: Trajectory-length control for bounded descent sequences.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, and the bounded sequence \((x_k)\) has a cluster point \(\bar x\) with \(f(x_k)\to f(\bar x)\).
For some \(a,b>0\), eventually \(f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge a\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x_{k+1}))\le b\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\).
The function \(f\) has the Kurdyka--Łojasiewicz property at every cluster point of \((x_k)\).

notation.meaning: distance from a point to a set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard abstract KL finite-length theorem under sufficient decrease and relative error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract finite-dimensional KL descent theorem for a bounded trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the stated descent, relative-error, continuity, and Kurdyka--Łojasiewicz assumptions, the trajectory has finite length: \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|<\infty.\] Consequently, \((x_k)\) is Cauchy and cannot move indefinitely among distinct cluster points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded KL descent sequence satisfying sufficient decrease and relative error has summable step lengths and therefore is Cauchy.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Length Convergence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the finite-length container and is recognizable as the standard finite-dimensional abstract KL descent result. However, no inspectable source is cited for the precise sufficient-decrease, relative-error, continuity, and KL hypotheses. The explanatory sentence about excluding motion among cluster points should also be checked against the eventual-hypothesis formulation once a source is supplied.

children.title: Whole-Sequence Critical-Point Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence of the complete iterate sequence rather than only subsequences.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subsequential Criticality Does Not Imply Whole-Sequence Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing that critical cluster points alone do not provide the finite-length or Cauchy mechanism required for whole-sequence convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(f\equiv0\), and let \(x_k=(-1)^k\). Then \(f(x_k)\) is nonincreasing, \(0\in\partial f(x_k)\) for every \(k\), and every cluster point is critical, but \((x_k)\) does not converge and \(\sum_k|x_{k+1}-x_k|=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded sequence can have nonincreasing objective values and only critical cluster points while still failing to converge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{cluster}(x_k)=\{-1,1\},\qquad x_k\not\to\bar x,\qquad \sum_k|x_{k+1}-x_k|=+\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Subsequential Criticality Does Not Imply Whole-Sequence Convergence

assumptions_latex: The subdifferential graph is closed along the sequence: if \(x_{k_j}\to x\), \(f(x_{k_j})\to f(x)\), and \(v_{k_j}\in\partial f(x_{k_j})\to v\), then \(v\in\partial f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_k\to\bar x\quad\text{and}\quad 0\in\partial f(\bar x).\]

notation.meaning: the unique limit of the complete sequence

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard whole-sequence consequence of KL finite length and subdifferential closedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Whole-sequence convergence following the abstract finite-length KL theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Finite length makes \((x_k)\) Cauchy, so in \(\mathbb{R}^n\) the entire sequence converges to its cluster point \(\bar x\). The relative-error inequality gives \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x_{k+1}))\to0\). Closedness of the subdifferential graph along the convergent values then yields \[x_k\to\bar x\qquad\text{and}\qquad 0\in\partial f(\bar x).\] Thus convergence is not merely subsequential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite length forces the complete iterate sequence to converge, and relative error plus subdifferential closedness makes its limit critical.
knowledge_statements.title: Whole-Sequence Critical-Point Convergence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role and complete-sequence conclusion fit the terminal container. Its validity depends on the preceding finite-length theorem and on the precise closedness property of the selected limiting subdifferential, but neither dependency has an inspectable citation. The statement also narrates the derivation rather than only recording the result.

children.title: Desingularization Rate Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: The rate taxonomy associated with local desingularization geometry.

children.title: Finite-Termination Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local desingularization regimes associated with finite termination.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Step Bound in the KL-Exponent-Zero Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative termination bound under explicitly normalized abstract descent and KL inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\to\bar x\) and \(r_k=f(x_k)-f(\bar x)\ge0\). From some index \(K\), suppose that whenever \(r_{k+1}>0\), \[r_k-r_{k+1}\ge a\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x_{k+1}))\le b\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|,\] and the exponent-zero KL inequality is normalized as \[c\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x_{k+1}))\ge1,\] where \(a,b,c>0\). Then a zero residual is reached at an index \(L\) satisfying \[L-K\le\left\lceil\frac{r_Kb^2c^2}{a}\right\rceil.\] If sufficient decrease continues and \(x_k\to\bar x\), then \(x_k=\bar x\) for every \(k\ge L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At KL exponent zero, every positive-residual step consumes a fixed amount of objective decrease, giving a finite bound on the steps remaining before the limiting point is reached.
assumptions_latex: The exponent-zero KL inequality holds with the displayed normalization and constant \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists L\le K+\left\lceil r_Kb^2c^2/a\right\rceil\;\forall k\ge L:\quad r_k=0,\quad x_k=\bar x.\)

notation.meaning: sufficient-decrease, relative-error, and normalized KL constants

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Step Bound in the KL-Exponent-Zero Regime

assumptions_latex: The abstract descent hypotheses hold near a limit \(\bar x\), with residual \(r_k:=f(x_k)-f(\bar x)\ge0\).
The KL inequality admits \(\varphi(s)=c s^{1-\theta}\) with \(c>0\) and exponent \(\theta=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists K<\infty\ \forall k\ge K:\quad r_k=0,\quad x_k=\bar x.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard KL exponent-zero termination regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination for the exponent-zero KL regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the power desingularizer \(\varphi(s)=c s^{1-\theta}\), the endpoint \(\theta=0\) makes the KL slope bound uniform away from the critical level. Combined with sufficient decrease and relative error, this excludes infinitely many nonzero steps near \(\bar x\). Hence there is an index \(K<\infty\) such that \[r_k=0\quad\text{and}\quad x_k=\bar x\qquad(k\ge K).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With KL exponent zero, sufficient decrease and relative error force the iterates to reach the limiting critical point after finitely many steps.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Termination Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A theorem is the appropriate kind for this finite-termination leaf, and the exponent-zero regime is standard. An authoritative KL-rate source is still required to confirm that the referenced abstract descent hypotheses suffice for eventual equality of both the residual and the iterates with the designated limit.

children.title: Linear-Rate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local geometric regimes associated with linear convergence.

assumptions_latex: The abstract descent hypotheses hold near \(\bar x\), and \(r_k:=f(x_k)-f(\bar x)\ge0\).
The KL inequality admits \(\varphi(s)=c s^{1-\theta}\) with \(c>0\) and \(0<\theta\le\tfrac12\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[r_k\le Cq^k,\qquad \|x_k-\bar x\|\le C' q^{k/2}\quad(k\ge k_0)\] for some \(C,C'>0\) and \(q\in(0,1)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard KL linear-rate regime under quadratic sufficient decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric objective convergence for KL exponents through one half.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KL exponents between zero and one half yield geometric objective decay and R-linear convergence of the iterates.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Rate Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind correctly matches the rate-regime container, and the stated geometric residual and R-linear iterate rates are consistent with the usual KL exponent convention. No source is provided for the exact descent interface or the claimed iterate-rate conversion, so the mathematical version remains source-dependent.

children.title: Sublinear-Rate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local geometric regimes associated with sublinear convergence.

assumptions_latex: The abstract descent hypotheses hold near \(\bar x\), and \(r_k:=f(x_k)-f(\bar x)\ge0\).
The KL inequality admits \(\varphi(s)=c s^{1-\theta}\) with \(c>0\) and \(\tfrac12<\theta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[r_k=O\!\left(k^{-1/(2\theta-1)}\right),\qquad \|x_k-\bar x\|=O\!\left(k^{-(1-\theta)/(2\theta-1)}\right).\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard KL polynomial-rate regime under quadratic sufficient decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial rates for KL exponents strictly above one half.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
When \(\tfrac12<\theta<1\), the KL descent recursion gives the polynomial bounds \[r_k=O\!\left(k^{-1/(2\theta-1)}\right),
\qquad
\|x_k-\bar x\|=O\!\left(k^{-(1-\theta)/(2\theta-1)}\right).\] The first estimate measures objective residual, while the second follows from the remaining trajectory length. Both exponents deteriorate as \(\theta\) approaches \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KL exponents above one half yield polynomial, rather than geometric, decay of objective residuals and iterate errors.
knowledge_statements.title: Sublinear-Rate Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits this leaf, and the displayed polynomial exponents match the standard quadratic-decrease and linear-relative-error KL taxonomy. The exact assumptions are only referenced abstractly and no authoritative rate citation is supplied.

children.title: Rate-Regime Transition Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Geometric thresholds separating the principal convergence-rate classes.

assumptions_latex: The KL desingularizer has power form \(\varphi(s)=c s^{1-\theta}\) with \(c>0\) and \(0\le\theta<1\).
The descent interface uses quadratic sufficient decrease and a linear relative-error bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\theta=0\ \text{separates finite termination from asymptotic convergence},\qquad \theta=\tfrac12\ \text{separates geometric from polynomial guarantees}.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: boundaries follow from the standard KL exponent taxonomy for the stated descent model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transition points for the quadratic-decrease, linear-relative-error KL taxonomy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the specified descent interface, the KL exponent partitions the rate guarantees as follows: \[\theta=0:\ \text{finite termination},\qquad
0<\theta\le\tfrac12:\ \text{geometric convergence},\qquad
\tfrac12<\theta<1:\ \text{polynomial convergence}.\] Hence \(0\) and \(\tfrac12\) are the transition boundaries; the inclusion of \(\tfrac12\) in the geometric regime depends on the quadratic-decrease and linear-relative-error powers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the standard KL descent powers, exponent zero marks finite termination and exponent one half separates geometric from polynomial rates.
knowledge_statements.title: Rate-Regime Transition Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind is suitable for a transition-boundary leaf, and the boundaries at zero and one half are internally consistent with the neighboring records. A source is required because these boundaries depend on the precise KL exponent convention and on the powers in the descent and relative-error interface.

children.title: Error-Robust Descent Interface
children.top_down_role: Extensions accommodating deterministic errors and perturbed descent relations.

children.title: Inexact Descent Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Local convergence interfaces accommodating controlled deterministic errors.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, and \(x_{k+1}\ne x_k\) is allowed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge a\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2-\eta_k,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x_{k+1}))\le b\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|+\zeta_k.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: common summably inexact sufficient-decrease and relative-error interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summably inexact version of the abstract KL descent interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence satisfies the summably inexact descent interface when constants \(a,b>0\) and nonnegative summable errors \((\eta_k)\), \((\zeta_k)\) exist such that, for every \(k\), \[f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge a\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2-\eta_k,\] \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x_{k+1}))\le b\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|+\zeta_k.\] The first error measures loss of descent; the second measures inexact stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact descent interface allows summable defects in both sufficient decrease and the relative stationarity estimate.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Descent Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A condition is the correct role for this interface. The two summable-defect inequalities form a plausible inexact model, but no source supports this particular combination, and the record does not explicitly introduce the iterate sequence as lying in the effective domain where all displayed quantities are meaningful.

children.title: Perturbed Descent Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Local convergence interfaces accommodating perturbations of descent relations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth perturbation model tied explicitly to an exact descent trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y_k=T_k(x_k)\) be an exact trial point satisfying \[f(y_k)\le f(x_k)-a\|y_k-x_k\|^2,\qquad \|\nabla f(y_k)\|\le b\|y_k-x_k\|.\] A relative-error perturbed update has the form \[x_{k+1}=y_k+e_k,\qquad \|e_k\|\le\theta\|y_k-x_k\|\] for a fixed \(\theta\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative-error perturbed descent update adds an error controlled by the exact descent step, whose decrease and stationarity properties are explicitly specified.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable on a neighborhood containing \(x_k\), \(y_k\), and \(x_{k+1}\).
The exact trial \(y_k=T_k(x_k)\) satisfies the displayed decrease and gradient-residual estimates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}=T_k(x_k)+e_k\quad\text{with}\quad\|e_k\|\le\theta\|T_k(x_k)-x_k\|.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Error Perturbed Descent Update

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transfer of Relative Update Error to Descent and Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth quantitative transfer from an exact descent trial to the implemented perturbed iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on the relevant segments and the relative-error update conditions hold. If \(\theta<1\) and \[c:=a-b\theta-\tfrac{L}{2}\theta^2>0,\] then \[f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge\frac{c}{(1+\theta)^2}\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\] and \[\|\nabla f(x_{k+1})\|\le\frac{b+L\theta}{1-\theta}\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth objective, a sufficiently small relative update error preserves sufficient decrease and a relative stationarity estimate with explicit degraded constants.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on each segment joining \(y_k\) and \(x_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge\frac{a-b\theta-(L/2)\theta^2}{(1+\theta)^2}\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2,\quad \|\nabla f(x_{k+1})\|\le\frac{b+L\theta}{1-\theta}\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|.

notation.meaning: local Lipschitz constant of the gradient

knowledge_statements.title: Transfer of Relative Update Error to Descent and Stationarity

assumptions_latex: Each exact iteration map \(T_k:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is defined at \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_{k+1}=T_k(x_k)+e_k,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|x_{k+1}-T_k(x_k)\|<\infty.\]

notation.meaning: exact iteration map at step k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard absolutely summable additive-perturbation interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive perturbations of an abstract exact iteration map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The perturbed iteration interface is \[x_{k+1}=T_k(x_k)+e_k,\] where \(T_k(x_k)\) is the exact update and \(e_k\) is the implementation or oracle perturbation. Absolute summability, \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|e_k\|<\infty,\] is the admissibility requirement ensuring finite cumulative displacement relative to the exact updates. Equivalently, \(\sum_k\|x_{k+1}-T_k(x_k)\|<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A perturbed iteration is admissible when its additive deviations from exact updates have finite total norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Perturbed Descent Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits an iteration interface, and the equivalence with absolute summability of the additive deviations is algebraically correct. A source is needed for treating this generic perturbed-map condition as a perturbed descent interface, since no descent or stationarity property of the maps is stated.

children.title: Error-Robust Rate Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer of tame geometric rates under admissible error.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualitative convergence and error-floor consequences of the scalar perturbed-contraction recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r_{k+1}\le q r_k+\varepsilon_k\), with \(r_k,\varepsilon_k\ge0\) and \(0<q<1\), \[\limsup_{k\to\infty}r_k\le \frac{\limsup_{k\to\infty}\varepsilon_k}{1-q}.\] In particular, \(\varepsilon_k\to0\) implies \(r_k\to0\); if \(\varepsilon_k\le E\), then \[r_k\le q^k r_0+\frac{E(1-q^k)}{1-q}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing forcing preserves convergence to zero, while uniformly bounded forcing yields a computable asymptotic error floor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \limsup_{k\to\infty}r_k\le (1-q)^{-1}\limsup_{k\to\infty}\varepsilon_k
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing and Uniform Forcing Transfer

assumptions_latex: A nonnegative residual obeys \(r_{k+1}\le q r_k+\varepsilon_k\) for some \(q\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[r_k\le q^k r_0+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}q^{k-1-j}\varepsilon_j;\] geometrically or polynomially decaying errors transfer their corresponding rate to \((r_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar perturbed-contraction mechanism underlying robust rate transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Iterating the perturbed contraction gives \[r_k\le q^k r_0+
\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}q^{k-1-j}\varepsilon_j.\] If \(\varepsilon_k\le C\rho^k\), then \(r_k=O(\max\{q,\rho\}^k)\) when \(q\ne\rho\), while \(r_k=O(kq^k)\) when \(q=\rho\). If \(\varepsilon_k=O(k^{-p})\) for \(p>0\), then \(r_k=O(k^{-p})\). Thus the slower of contraction and error decay determines the transferred rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A perturbed contraction inherits the slower of its exact contraction rate and the decay rate of its additive errors.
knowledge_statements.title: Error-Robust Rate Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar convolution estimate and its geometric and polynomial consequences are mathematically standard. For this rate-transfer terminal, the record is more precisely a complexity bound than a generic property, and a source is required to justify its mapping to the surrounding inexact optimization interfaces.

children.title: Perturbation Admissibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Error regimes that no longer preserve descent-based convergence conclusions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of convergence to zero under a nonvanishing additive perturbation in a contractive recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<q<1\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and \(r_0=0\). The recursion \[r_{k+1}=q r_k+\varepsilon\] satisfies \[r_k=\frac{\varepsilon(1-q^k)}{1-q}\longrightarrow\frac{\varepsilon}{1-q}>0.\] Thus bounded but nonvanishing forcing does not preserve convergence of the residual to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant additive error in a contractive recursion produces a positive error floor rather than convergence to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_k\to\varepsilon/(1-q)>0
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Forcing Error Floor

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_k=\sum_{j=1}^{k}\frac1j\to+\infty,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}|x_{k+1}-x_k|=\infty.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: harmonic-series counterexample establishes the claimed summability boundary
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Square summability alone does not control cumulative perturbation displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Vanishing, square-summable perturbations need not be admissible for conclusions requiring finite cumulative displacement. Indeed, with \(x_0=0\) and \[x_{k+1}=x_k+\frac1{k+1},\] one has \(e_k\to0\) and \(\sum_k e_k^2<\infty\), but \[x_k=\sum_{j=1}^{k}\frac1j\to+\infty,
\qquad
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}|x_{k+1}-x_k|=\infty.\] Thus replacing absolute summability by square summability cannot generally preserve boundedness or finite length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Harmonic perturbations vanish and are square summable, yet their cumulative displacement diverges; absolute summability cannot generally be dropped.
knowledge_statements.title: Perturbation Admissibility Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind exactly fits the container, and the harmonic-increment counterexample correctly separates square summability from absolute summability and finite cumulative displacement. Under the supplied evidence discipline, the record still lacks a source reference despite being elementary and is already marked needs_source.
